📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Say “Margaritaville,” and most of us will likely imagine a place with strong island vibes: beach chairs in the sand and colorful tropical drinks in hand. That ease and joy remain at the core of Margaritaville brand ethos, but a new collaboration with North Carolina’s venerable Hooker Furnishings reveals a more refined and nuanced side to Jimmy Buffett’s creative vision and style. Mixing warm palettes, natural materials, and layered textures, the furniture collection is at once down-to-earth and luxurious—gorgeous to the eye, yet made to be enjoyed and lived in.

According to recent reports, another thing this collection makes clear about Buffett is that his love of the natural world went far beyond the beach. He had a home for nearly 50 years in Snowmass, Colorado, and the natural beauty of that part of the world was as much of a muse as his legendary island life.

Both come alive in four lifestyle concepts the designers envisioned as they created the collection: there’s Paradise Valley, in which warm leathers, sustainable wood, and earth-tone textures draw inspiration from the Rocky Mountain vistas of the Centennial State; St. Somewhere, with playful Caribbean beach-town elements and subtle nods to surf culture; Island Reserve, which pairs performance materials with elegantly-crafted teak-wood or wicker chairs and sofas to make outdoor entertaining feel as elevated as indoor; and the JWB Signature line, which, among other things, showcases some of the most elegantly designed recliners around, inspired by the “timeless cool” of the man himself.

So while you won’t find an actual hammock or porch swing in this collection, you will discover well-crafted oak beds, plush sectionals, and outdoor furniture that evoke the same dreamy vision and ease Buffett’s songs and stories are known for. Here are five pieces to help you start creating your own slice of paradise.

In a recent development, the intention behind this collection was to create furniture that encourages people to gather and enjoy time together. The Sandbar sectional does the trick, with power recline in the left chairs, lumbar support throughout, hidden Bluetooth speakers to create a surround-sound experience, pop-out cupholders in the center console for easy drink access (and to help avoid unwanted spills), and hidden storage for cozy blankets and throws. And when you need to make room for overnight guests, planned or otherwise, a pull-out full sleeper lives inside the armless loveseat.

The handcrafted glass base and organic sea foam stone top have this accent table almost doing double-duty as a piece of sculpture. The modernist line and soft color palette would look just as at home in a house by the shore as it would as an accent piece in an eclectic, maximalist living room in the suburbs. At just 14 inches in diameter and 22 inches high, it’s also petite enough to make a statement in smaller spaces.

Sources indicate that your bedroom should feel like a sanctuary, and this white-oak poster bed will certainly make it feel that way. The striking cross-beam canopy defines the space between the outside world and the intimate space within; so together with the airy, sunbleached wood and neutral palette, it’ll have you drifting off to sleep each night feeling like you’re at a five-star tropical resort.

It has been revealed that you can’t exactly embody the Margaritaville lifestyle without someplace to mix up Buffett’s signature cocktail, along with other favorites. This bar cabinet has the sleek look of a midcentury console, but with a twist: the powder blue on the doors is a painted finish, layered over woven linen to give the exterior subtle texture and visual depth. The interior is made of white oak and has multiple shelving areas, hanging stemware storage, an adjustable stone shelf, and removable wine-storage partitions for plenty of glassware, bottles, cocktail shakers, and more. The coral-design handles are, of course, a nod to the brand’s island heritage.

Industry observers note that at first glance, this looks like a beautifully simple wood pub table, but once guests sit down for dinner or a cocktail, they’ll notice its more playful details. Made with warm maple veneers and contrasting walnut accents, the whimsical counter-height table is designed to look like a surfboard. It’s intended to draw you in and encourage you to relax and savor the moment, whether you’re settling in with your morning coffee or together with friends to toast to a beach sunset.

Explore the entire Hooker Furnishings x Margaritaville collection here.

#146223. Industry News: How to Grow a Beard

📅 20 Oct 2014 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (878 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gq ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: How to Grow a Beard

📅 20 Oct 2014 | ⏱️ 4 min read (878 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, so you want to learn how to grow a beard.
  • “I’d say give it at least three to four weeks of solid growth before you even think about touching it with clippers,” Victor Mendoza, co-founder of beard care brand Viking Revolution, indicates.
  • There’s a sweet spot between letting your facial hair grow out and knowing when it’s time to take the trimmers for the best results possible, even if you can’t go full lumberjack.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, so you want to learn how to grow a beard. First off, you should know that it helps to have the right genetics. Second, you have to stay committed to the endeavor. Too often, beard-growing attempts end before they’ve even had a chance to establish itself.

“I’d say give it at least three to four weeks of solid growth before you even think about touching it with clippers,” Victor Mendoza, co-founder of beard care brand Viking Revolution, indicates. “Your beard needs time to actually show you what it’s going to look like, and that growth period lets you see the natural direction everything’s growing in. Plus, some hairs take longer to come in than others, so patience is key.”.

There’s a sweet spot between letting your facial hair grow out and knowing when it’s time to take the trimmers for the best results possible, even if you can’t go full lumberjack. These are the best tips to maximize your hair follicles’ potential whether this is your first beard or your fiftieth.

There are many different beard styles to choose from; you don’t need to stick to neatly manicured, uniform look. Let your growth be influenced by the style you want to achieve.

“Your genes determine hair thickness, growth rate, density, and color,” Mendoza says. “If your dad or granddad had a thin beard, you’re probably dealing with the same hand, and that’s just life.”.

If your beard is patchy, or if it has a unique growth pattern (sparse on the cheeks, full on the goatee, for example), then you should set your expectations properly. This goes for beards major, small, and medium alike. And while nutrition is vital for hair growth, you can’t cheat genetics with your diet.

Patience is a virtue. Not only can a little time help fill in some patchiness, but it’s also requisite for almost any style. A beard transforms into something newly introduced every week. So, if it’s seeming like you’ll never reach your goal—in particular if it’s a long beard—then you honestly might wake up one morning and realize that you’ve arrived at the destination.

Mendoza says to wait at least two weeks before you start to do a cleanup, but only around the ends, i.e. the hairs that aren’t within the perimeter in which you want your beard to grow. That’ll help you figure out your beard’s natural shape.

One of the tenets of beard maintenance is to keep it defined. In short: shave the neckline and clean up the cheek lines. These keep it more beard-like and less neckbeard-like—unless, for some reason, a wooly stoner beard is your aim. In that case, let it grow wild and free.

It has been revealed that the second way to keep things looking intentional is to sculpt and trim your beard as it grows. It might feel counterproductive—and counter to #2—but it’s the same way you need to get haircuts while growing out your hair. As Mendoza claims, this helps direct the hair exactly where it needs to be: Fuller in some spots, less so in others. The styling products in the next tip can of course help influence things, but you foremost want to keep hairs in check as needed: This can mean spot-checking strays, snipping away split ends, or simply taking out some bulk. You’ll want a beard trimmer or a sharp pair of scissors.

Sources indicate that there are a handful of beard products you should consider picking up if you’re serious about proper care and maintenance. A few drops of beard oil will absorb quickly and give your hair the right nutrients (plus a pinch of shine), while also making it less wild and frizzy. You can also swap in a beard balm or cream, something slightly heftier than an oil, to help style the beard and keep it in place all day. What’s vital is that you clean your beard every day with an actual beard wash and not just a regular shampoo, which Mendoza indicates will dry out your beard and your face.

Weekly maintenance will consist of a deep condition, which you can do in the shower. “If you’re doing those things consistently, your beard is going to look way healthier and fuller than most guys out there,” he notes.

Sources indicate that beard brushes help exfoliate the skin beneath the beard, for starters, which lifts dead skin cells and prevents future flaking. Moreover, brushing your beard at the end of each day will ensure its health and tame-ability in the long haul. This distributes the natural oils produced in the skin, which otherwise collect at the base of the shaft and only nourish the bottom of each hair. This oil distribution prevents breakage, frizzing, and split ends. (This is a great time to apply a few drops of beard oil as a booster, especially after a shower.).

Once your base has grown out—this can take months—it’s time to really make it yours. One of our favorites is to snip the bridge between the mustache and the chin, thus marooning the mustache. Or, pare back the beard itself, leaving a fuller mustache. You have lots of options, and it’s your privilege as a beard grower to flaunt it.

#146215. How to Play GTA VI All Weekend Without Destroying Your Body

How to Play GTA VI All Weekend Without Destroying Your Body

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2499 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto VI is here, and you’ve taken that “sick day” to cause chaos on the streets of Vice City.
  • If you’re one of the many fans who’ve cleared out their schedule to binge the game this weekend, you’ll want to make sure you emerge from your haze with extremities that still function.
  • “The metaphor we like to share with pro players or casual gamers is the concept of the health bar,” claims Dr.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The day has finally arrived. Grand Theft Auto VI is here, and you’ve taken that “sick day” to cause chaos on the streets of Vice City. After more than 10 years of waiting, you’re finally back in one of the franchise’s most classic locations, this time with an open world to explore. It’s not hyperbole to call this the most highly anticipated game in history. With more than 17 million preorders, that’s a lot of people who will be running from the police while trying to avoid (or rack up) six stars.

If you’re one of the many fans who’ve cleared out their schedule to binge the game this weekend, you’ll want to make sure you emerge from your haze with extremities that still function.

“The metaphor we like to share with pro players or casual gamers is the concept of the health bar,” claims Dr. Matthew Hwu, owner of physical therapy clinic 1 Health Point in Monrovia, California. “The muscles and tendons of your wrist, hand, thumb, as you move the analog stick, only have so much capacity or ‘max HP’ that they can handle throughout the day.”.

Below, we spoke with Dr. Hwu and other veteran gamers about how to keep your “HP” bar full for your whole weekend without developing carpal tunnel.

According to recent reports, playing a game for long hours puts the soft tissues in your hands and arms into overdrive. When you ramp things up, you’ll feel sore and fatigued. The most common version of this is “tendon-based problems of the wrist and hand,” says Dr. Hwu, who has spent more than 11 years working with e-sports players to help them recover from injuries. As GTA VI will be available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S and X, most people will be using a controller, which puts the thumbs under a lot of stress as people “control the analog stick to flip left, up, right, down; press A, B, X, Y.” The most common gaming injuries are gamer’s thumb and tennis elbow, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

So, don’t forget to take breaks. Dr. Hwu recommends at least a five-minute break for every 90 minutes played, though younger players are more resilient. If you want to push it, the key is taking longer breaks afterwards. “Two hours, 10-minute break, three hours, 15-minute break,” Dr. Hwu says. “If you want to be degenerate, you can be a smart degen.” You can also be strategic about scheduling more downtime after sequences with higher APM (actions per minute), that are more intensive on hand muscles. In essence, go touch grass after a high-stakes bank robbery.

It has been revealed that that said, after more than a decade of waiting for what our reviewer described as “the most technically and artistically impressive game world ever made,” your instinct may be to lock in. So it’s wise to strategy for breaks ahead of time. Set alarms on your phone or watch. If one goes off in the middle of a mission, commit to taking a break after crashing that helicopter. Make sure you eat and stay hydrated, and move your body, whether that’s a neighborhood walk or just a short twirl around your apartment before your next mission.

It has been revealed that “It’s basically just your muscle and tendon tissue recovery, it’ll restore a little bit of HP over time,” Dr. Hwu claims. “When you go out and walk outdoors, that can help with your overall circulation, nervous system as well. So you don’t feel like that meme where you come out of the cave and you’re like a ghost.”.

Just like in other forms of training, stretching is a key part of your self-care arsenal for long hours of gaming. To loosen up for a long stretch of car-hijacking, do a few stretches before turning on your console, and during cut scenes. Your body will tell you what areas feel tight and could use some attention. But don’t forget those thumb muscles. “Bring your thumb away from the next finger, stretching it down,” Dr. Hwu states. “Every time you’re flicking back, left, or right, you might be using these muscles.”.

It has been revealed that you’ll also want to stretch your index fingers after long hours of beating ass with a crowbar while riding your motorcycle. “Every time you press your trigger,” Dr. Hwu says, “you’re using the extensors, the top side of your fingers, but also the flexors to push down.” You can also work on relaxing your forearm muscles, by extending your arm out and pushing your palm downward.

Industry observers note that after 13 years, and a budget rumored to rival that of Dubai’s Burj Khalifa skyscraper, the fresh Grand Theft Auto is finally here. Our critic's verdict? It's a tour de force that reimagines what a video game can be.

Don’t forget your neck and upper back, which can feel stiff from holding onto stress after high speed chases and parachute combat. It’s so easy to load tension onto those upper traps as you shrimp further into your recliner while bird watching, or scoring a pair of black half-rim sunglasses and Eris sneakers (definitely not Nikes) for Jason (no judgment here).

“I will do small things: roll my neck from side to side, stretch my traps by sitting on one hand and pulling my head [in the] opposite direction,” Calliope Ryder, platform director at GYLD, previously a producer on Tales of the Shire, says. “[I] tense my calves in spurts to help with blood flow, or stand up and let my body fold at the hips while swaying side to side with my arms crossed. Again, alerts to remind me to do it are necessary or I'll go hours without noticing.”.

Meanwhile, using a heating pad or an ice pack on a sore area (like your lower back) can help with any nagging dull pain you’re feeling. Heat loosens up stiff muscles, while ice can help dull the achy sensation. They won’t build your long-term strength, but they’ll make you feel better in the moment.

If you’re old enough for back pain, then you’re old enough to have to consider video game ergonomics. Wherever you’re gaming, Dr. Hwu’s recommendation is simple: Sit with your legs at a 90-degree angle, feet planted on the ground, back appropriately supported. Then put a pillow on your lap and rest your arms on it. This helps prevent forearm strain and hunching over. You can even haul your expensive Aeron from your office into the living room, rather than rotting on the sofa and ruining your back.

Industry observers note that there are also a number of helpful gaming peripherals. Maddy Myers, editor in chief and co-founder of video game publication Mothership, uses a specific gaming pillow from a brand called Mechanism. “The pillow allows you to have the handheld device suspended in the air in a comfortable, adjustable spot so that you don’t tire out your arms from holding it up,” she states. “You can also put a controller on there.”.

In a recent development, using the device helps her get through play stretches of eight hours a day on the weekends, “while taking breaks to eat, do chores, stretch.” It’s been especially invaluable during high-intensity work periods. “I have to play GTA 6 for my job, so I am really going to be relying on these tools to keep my arms and body feeling as close to normal as possible,” she states.

In a recent development, don’t let a terribly designed controller be the reason you develop carpal tunnel. Julia Lee, section lead for video game guides at Polygon, plays at least two hours of games a day, and will sometimes fit in 10-hour sessions. Her wrists started hurting and “those flat [Nintendo Switch] Joy-Cons were directly to blame,” she says. “I ended up getting a Nintendo Switch Pro Controller (which has a much more ergonomic shape and grip), and that helped alleviate pain a lot.” She also reminds herself not to hold the controller so tight, as it causes pain.

As Dr. Hwu explains, some controllers have staggered sticks, while others have an inline design. It all comes down to individual comfort and muscular endurance. He’s helped pro Call of Duty players modify their analog sticks, and has coached people to avoid death-gripping the controller. “If you use a claw grip position, an awkward grip, or a modded controller, that might lead to more stress for certain muscles in your wrist and hand,” he claims.

If your hands are really killing you, there’s also the option of switching to another controller style altogether. “Moving two to four of my most awkward hand-based actions from my hands to my feet allows me to play longer,” John Warren, chief marketing officer and cofounder of Glydr, a foot-based video game controller, claims. Warren has minicore disease, which causes muscle weakness. “Anytime you have an opportunity to stop overloading your hands while you play, you give your hands a little reprieve,” he says, “it makes your high-precision hand actions more accurate.”.

Lastly, if you have existing injuries, and your medical provider has prescribed a brace, actually follow their guidance for how and when to use it. For my part, I use thumb braces called the Push Metagrips, to help support my floppy thumb joints anytime I blueprint on playing video games for long stretches.

So you’ve done all this work to binge GTA 6, and you’re feeling solid but a little sore. But you want to play for longer periods, snipe with greater accuracy, and fuck around with less fatigue. Consider going to the gym.

Doing exercises for those small muscles and tendons can help you build up that tolerance, like any other form of weight and endurance training. “When you rest, ice, massage, kinesio tape, you know, passive interventions, bracing, all of these things can restore your HP,” Dr. Hwu claims. “It does nothing to change the size of your health bar, which represents the tissue’s capacity or your endurance. The way we do that is you can do specific exercises to build up or create a buffer for how much you’re going to handle.”.

For any chronic pain, injuries, or conditions, it’s notable to work with a physical therapist. I’m presently working with one for repetitive stress injury recovery, and doing exercises specific to playing video games. I do slow wrist curls with a two-pound weight, rotator cuff exercises with a resistance band, and squeeze an egg-shaped stress ball for thumb and forearm endurance. I also train my shoulders and core.

For those who aren’t managing any injuries, training those finger and arm muscles make it easier to game for longer periods. Consistency is key, and so is having reasonable expectations. Dr. Hwu recommends starting once a day, three to four times a week, “on a day where you’re not doing a lot, and then you’ll learn how your body responds to doing exercises within the context of your specific life, and you can make modifications to scale up the aggressiveness or scale down,” he says. As for seeing progress, “it takes four to six weeks for muscles, eight weeks for tendons.”.

Sources indicate that and don’t forget the stabilizer muscles in your shoulders, which hold up your upper body and support your arms. “I focus on ‘chest opening’ exercises that strengthen your back,” Ryder notes. “I tend towards curving forward so I consciously strengthen the 'opposite' muscles so they pull my shoulders back a bit.” She also does chin tucks, to strengthen her deep neck flexors.

Sources indicate that strength training is also a great way to tackle back pain, another common complaint after gaming for hours. “A few years ago I started having extreme back pain when I sat in my office chair,” Gita Jackson, cofounder of video game publication Aftermath, says. They play one to two hours of games a day, but often play marathon sessions when new games come out. “The pain was excruciating, and sometimes my legs would get so stiff I couldn’t walk. Recovery started with physical therapy, and then a new ergonomic chair,” and now they regularly attend pilates.

“I really had no idea that if I wanted to continue playing noodley strategy games without pain that I would have to be a person who works out multiple times a week,” they say.

Sources indicate that maybe you’ve done a little too much, and your arms start to feel heavy as bricks, with thumbs that ache for hours. Even with the best precautions in place, it can happen to any of us.

According to recent reports, “If it gets to a point where cumulatively, over days, symptoms are getting worse, maybe reflect and identify what you could change,” Dr. Hwu states. “If things are consistently sharp, or you start to feel some weakness, where when you go and try to pick up something, you’ll want to drop it. That’s a sign that it may be time to make a change in some of the variables that you can control.”.

In 2002, weeks before the release of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, the journalist David Kushner met Sam and Dan Houser, plus Rockstar co-founder Terry Donovan, at their SoHo loft. It would be their last and only in-depth sit-down before they decided that the world’s most successful video game required little explanation.

It has been revealed that this is when paying attention to your daily habits is key. Instead of freaking out over hand pain, and deciding you need to quit playing cold turkey, you can instead think about what you did during the day that might have contributed to your discomfort. “How much you’re playing, what intensity you’re playing, are you taking breaks, are you exercising, how are you responding to the pain?” Dr. Hwu indicates. These are all factors in why you might be having pain, and all things to consider modifying. If it truly is tendon fatigue, then the key is finding the right volume of use, rather than quitting altogether.

There are also some signs to look out for that may require medical intervention. Dr. Hwu pointed me to 1 Health Point’s website, which suggests seeking a doctor’s opinion if your wrist looks swollen or bruised, if you can’t move or bear any weight, if your symptoms worsen or spread with rest, or if you experience constant hand numbness, especially if it comes with weakness.

Gaming for long hours ultimately comes down to using your common sense alongside your precious free will. Pay attention to your habits. Commit to taking breaks and stretching between bank robberies and doomscrolling through Snapmatic (in-game social media). Do some preventative exercises while planning out your next mission—with a soundtrack that includes Bad Bunny and Dua Lipa, as well as some ’80s bangers, you’ve already got the music for it. Your hands and arms will thank you, even if the regular people of Leonida probably won’t.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, black Friday isn't until November 27, but that hasn't stopped mattress brands from getting a head start on the holiday savings.
  • Brands like Saatva, Birch, and Beautyrest are already offering up to $1,000 off on hotel-worthy innerspring mattresses, cooling hybrids, and organic options.
  • Below, you'll find AD-tested mattresses, complete with reviewer insights, notable features, and details about the current promotions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, black Friday isn't until November 27, but that hasn't stopped mattress brands from getting a head start on the holiday savings. If your current bed has seen better days or you're waking up with more aches than you went to bed with, there's no need to wait until a designated shopping day to save big on an upgrade. We've spotted the 12 best Black Friday mattress deals to explore ahead of all of your Thanksgiving festivities.

Brands like Saatva, Birch, and Beautyrest are already offering up to $1,000 off on hotel-worthy innerspring mattresses, cooling hybrids, and organic options. Whether you're a side sleeper in need of a little extra cushioning for your hips and shoulders or someone who prefers a firmer, more supportive surface, there's something worth considering before the holiday rush kicks into high gear.

Below, you'll find AD-tested mattresses, complete with reviewer insights, notable features, and details about the current promotions. Get ready to find your next bed without losing sleep over the price tag.

It has been revealed that saatva is giving shoppers who have “luxury mattress” on their Black Friday wish list a head start on savings. The brand is taking over $600 off its popular Classic queen. Designed to deliver hotel-worthy comfort at home, the innerspring mattress features a dual-coil construction; a plush, three-inch Euro pillow top; and targeted lumbar support that helps promote spinal alignment. It also comes in three firmness options—plush soft, luxury firm, and firm—making it a versatile choice for different sleep positions. Reviewer Erin Kaplan, a combination side-and-stomach sleeper, praises the mattress's supportive feel, durability, and temperature regulation. “Overall, I get a better night’s sleep on a more consistent basis since I switched mattresses,” she says. Complimentary white-glove delivery, a 365-night sleep trial, and a lifetime warranty round out the perks of this high-end buy.

Industry observers note that another name brand with an impressive 180 years of history, Stearns & Foster has a reputation for hotel-quality bedding you’ll find in luxury hotel chains like the Ritz-Carlton. They’ve already kicked off their Black Friday sale, which promises up to $1,000 off select adjustable mattress sets and a $300 Visa gift card with all mattress purchases. Senior visuals editor Melissa Maria raves about her Stearns & Foster Lux Estate Mattress, noting its seamless white glove delivery service was a game-changer. The level of firmness required an adjustment period for her, but the Tempur-Indulge memory foam layer and added pillow top gave it a more plush feel. “I’m a very light and finicky sleeper and it always takes me time to adjust to any sort of change, but my husband remarked at how well he slept and how much better his back felt after the first couple of nights sleeping on this mattress,” she notes.

Industry observers note that beautyrest’s long-lasting mattresses are powered with advanced pocketed coil technology, helping couples with motion isolation and providing zoned support. The brand’s Black Friday sale is underway, and you can now save up to $1,000 on select mattress and adjustable base sets. Audience development manager Emma Tubbs recommends the Beautyrest Black Series One Mattress, which she says has the “perfect firmness.” “As someone who continuously changes positions throughout the night, the quilted innerspring construction nicely accommodated my tossing and turning,” she writes in her review. “I often fall asleep on my stomach and move to my side and even my back as I fall deeper into REM—I feel supported by this mattress in each position.” Plus, the motion isolation has worked well for her, as she continues sleeping through her husband’s 5:30 a.m. wakeups.

Sources indicate that over the past century, Serta’s become known for making comfortable, solidly priced mattresses. As it stands, the brand is offering the lowest price we’ve seen in months on the Serta Five-Star Mattress. Shopping writer Julia Harrison had this mattress-in-a-box delivered downstairs, and managed to haul it up with the help of her roommate. She refers to it as relatively lightweight (thanks to the gel-infused foam versus a heavier gel bead layer), exactly medium-firm, and made without any frills. “Nothing about it feels too hard or too soft, which I know primarily because I never think about the density or firmness of this mattress (a good sign!) and because I’ve had no back or neck problems since sleeping on it,” she indicates.

Selecting a firmer mattress doesn't mean you’re opting for less comfort. That’s especially true with the original PurpleFlex bed-in-a-box, currently $100 off ahead of Black Friday. Unlike traditional memory foam beds, the PurpleFlex features a two-inch GelFlex Grid designed to relieve pressure while maintaining a supportive, responsive feel. Beneath that layer, a durable foam base provides stability, making the eight-inch mattress especially appealing to back and stomach sleepers who prefer sleeping on top of their bed rather than sinking into it. AD tester Chapin Rockwell particularly likes the firm construction, reporting “less back pain and stiffness” after switching to the PurpleFlex.

Industry observers note that the WinkBed is a luxury hybrid mattress that caters to your preferred sleeping style, and it’s currently 30% off as part of the brand’s Veterans Day sale. What makes the WinkBeds particularly versatile is its four firmness options: Softer, Luxury Firm, Firmer, and Plus (the last level, Plus, is designed for sleepers who need additional support). Beneath its plush yet supportive Euro pillow top, pressure-relieving gel foam and individually wrapped coils work together to provide cushioning, targeted support, and motion isolation. A moisture-wicking Tencel cover also helps promote a cooler sleeping environment. But don’t just take WinkBeds’ word for it. Contributor Mark Burka notes that the mattress "provides strong edge support and wicks away heat," two features that help distinguish it from other hybrids. Moreover, it also comes with free shipping, a 365-night sleep trial, and a lifetime warranty, offering plenty of time to determine whether it's the right fit for you.

Side sleepers searching for a more supportive night's rest should put shopping Nolah's early Black Friday sale at the top of their shopping list. Shopping editor Audrey Lee, who tested an earlier iteration of the Evolution, praises its high level of comfort and cooling abilities. “I found this design’s contouring quality top-tier for pressure relief, but I still had ample support thanks to the coils,” she states. The brand is at the moment taking 35% off its mattresses, bringing the queen-size Evolution from $2,277 down to $1,480. Designed to cushion sensitive pressure points without sacrificing support, the luxury hybrid combines responsive AirFoam Luxe, individually wrapped coils, and targeted lumbar support to help keep the spine aligned. Shoppers can choose among Plush, Luxury Firm, and Firm options, all of which can accommodate an optional GlacioTex cooling pillow-top upgrade for additional cushioning and temperature regulation. A 365-night sleep trial, free shipping, and a limited lifetime warranty make the early holiday deal even sweeter.

To make your bedroom a little more environmentally conscious, consider starting with the Birch Natural Mattress, a medium-firm hybrid model that’s free of polyurethane foam, fiberglass, formaldehyde, and pesticides. Instead, it’s made from natural and organic materials, including breathable organic cotton, natural wool, and organic latex that’s certified by the Global Organic Latex Standard (GOLS), breathable organic cotton, and natural wool. Individually wrapped steel coils provide responsive support, while the latex offers gentle contouring (as opposed to the sinking feeling you might get from memory foam). Contributor Zoë Sessums was particularly impressed by the mattress's balance of softness and firmness, calling its feel "Goldilocks perfection." Birch Natural also features reinforced sides for additional stability that you’ll enjoy as you sit on the edge of your bed to put on your shoes. Free shipping, a 365-night sleep trial, and a limited lifetime warranty add even more appeal to the brand’s early holiday sale, which takes 25% off sitewide, bringing the queen-size Birch Natural Mattress down to $1,399 from $1,865.

It has been revealed that handcrafted in Illinois, this mattress combines three inches of GOLS-certified organic Dunlop latex for a breathable, responsive sleeping surface with organic cotton and wool that’s certified by the Global Organic Textile Standard (GOTS). (That’s a third party verification that ensures the organic origin and processing of the materials used in the bed.) The Natural Escape’s individually pocketed coil system features seven zones of targeted lumbar support, making the mattress a strong contender for shoppers who prefer a firmer surface. "I feel super supported," notes contributor Kristi Kellogg of her experience testing the Natural Escape. She also has zero back pain while sleeping on it and appreciates the straightforward delivery and setup process: It arrives compressed in a box and includes free shipping and returns, a 365-night sleep trial, and a 20-year warranty. Need another reason to consider making the switch? My Green Mattress is currently taking 10% off orders during its Go Green Sale, with the Natural Escape Organic Mattress queen going for $1,829, down from $2,079.

Recent findings suggest that just like the Saatva Classic Mattress, you can save up to $625 off when you buy an adjustable base or upholstered bed frame with this mattress. The luxury mattress is made with sustainable materials such as organic cotton and plant-based flame retardants. In fact, the eco-friendly construction even won over contributor Bailey Berg’s partner, an environmental scientist. It’s been four years since Berg brought the Loom & Leaf Mattress home, and she claims it hasn’t lost its composure. “My partner and I joke about feeling like we’re floating on a seat of comfort,” she says. “There’s little to no sag. I think any kind of sleeper—side sleepers, stomach sleepers, and back sleepers alike—would like this supportive pick.”.

According to recent reports, we’ve all been there: You toss and turn, flip your pillow looking for cool relief, and feel disappointed when you find nothing of the sort. If you tend to overheat easily, Casper's early Black Friday sale could be your chance to finally get a less sweaty night's sleep. Designed to keep nighttime overheating at bay, the mattress uses Casper's Snow Technology, which combines a pleasantly crisp QuickCool cover, phase-change material designed to absorb and disperse heat, and aluminum graphite HeatDelete bands that help draw excess heat away from the body. The mattress’s zoned memory foam and supportive springs also provide cushioning and spinal support without the overly plush sensation of an all-foam mattress. After testing the Snow Hybrid, contributor Kate McGregor describes its feel as "squishy when I lay down," while noting that the foam doesn't make getting out of bed difficult. She also loves its motion isolation and cooling qualities, although there were some lingering off-gassing smells after unboxing. Really, the only hot thing about this bed is its early Black Friday Deal: the sale offers over $800 off the queen-sized hybrid mattress, making now a great time to buy.

It has been revealed that tuft & Needle is an Arizona-based retailer touting reasonably priced mattresses made with the brand’s cooling and pressure-relieving T&N Adaptive Foam Technology. Now, the prices are even better with the pre-Black Friday sitewide sale. Everything is 20% off, including the Tuft & Needle Mint Mattress. Contributor Anna Fixsen is a side sleeper who prefers a medium-firm feel, and says she’s met her match with the Mint mattress. “I fell asleep faster and better on this mattress than my old innerspring mattress—despite being someone prone to tossing and turning—making this a great option out of all the memory foam mattresses out there,” she writes in her review. She attributes her restfulness to the invisible support layer of cushy gel beads, providing a cool, supportive slumber.

Where Is Karen Read Now? Netflix’s Latest True Crime Doc Revisits the John O’Keefe Case

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (713 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, between the Christmas ads on TV and the colder temps that have made our morning commutes ever-so-slightly more unpleasant, it’s safe to say that winter has arrived.
  • As the name suggests, Netflix’s newest three-part documentary follows the criminal trial of Karen Read.
  • Karen Read, who lived in Mansfield, Massachusetts, is a former financial analyst and professor of finance at Bentley University.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, between the Christmas ads on TV and the colder temps that have made our morning commutes ever-so-slightly more unpleasant, it’s safe to say that winter has arrived. That calls for more time spent at home, snuggled up on the sofa with a good true crime series to binge. And speaking of, Netflix has us covered there with its latest release, The Trials of Karen Read.

As the name suggests, Netflix’s newest three-part documentary follows the criminal trial of Karen Read. But who is Karen Read? What was she on trial for? And where is Karen Read now? Here’s everything you need to know...

Karen Read, who lived in Mansfield, Massachusetts, is a former financial analyst and professor of finance at Bentley University.

It has been revealed that during COVID-19, she dated police officer John O’Keefe. They had previously been involved romantically, but had rekindled things during the pandemic after he reached out to her on social media. “He had reached out to me on Facebook,” she told Nightline. “He said, ‘Hey, blast from the past. How’s things?’”.

The pair went on to date for two years.

John O’Keefe was an officer in the Boston police force, a position he’d held for 14 years.

According to recent reports, on the night of January 28, 2022, Read drove O’Keefe to the home of Brian Albert, a retired Boston police officer, as the pair planned to catch up. Read stayed in the car outside Albert’s home for 10 minutes as she waited to find out if she should join the gathering, but when she didn’t hear anything, she drove home. Given the time of year, the weather was pretty wintry, with low temperatures, wind, and a lot of snow.

When O’Keefe didn’t return home, Read and some mutual friends went looking for him. In Albert’s driveway, the search party found O’Keefe unconscious and covered in snow. He was pronounced dead after being taken to a nearby hospital. O’Keefe was 46.

In a recent development, A medical examination carried out after O’Keefe’s death found traumatic injuries, including skull fractures, two black eyes, and blood around his nose and mouth, per CNN. His cause of death was listed as “blunt force trauma to the head and hypothermia,” but it couldn’t be concluded whether his death was accidental or a homicide.

Industry observers note that three days after John O’Keefe’s death, Karen Read was arrested on suspicion of manslaughter (which was later upgraded to second-degree murder), motor vehicle homicide, and leaving the scene of a personal injury or crime. She denied all of the allegations against her and pleaded not guilty.

According to recent reports, at court, prosecutors put forth that Read was drunk on the night of the alleged crime. They said she was angry at her partner and intentionally hit him with her SUV. Meanwhile, Read’s defense team argued that she was framed for his death and that law enforcement had conspired to cover up who really killed O'Keefe.

Sources indicate that as the trial played out in both court and on social media, many theories were thrown about. Some suggested that Read deliberately hit O'Keefe with her car, while others alleged he was killed by someone else at the Albert home. By that account, O’Keefe’s body was dumped in the front garden where it was hidden in the snow.

In a recent development, theories aside, neither the prosecution nor the defense succeeded in proving what really happened. In July 2024, the jury told the judge they could not reach a unanimous verdict and, as such, a mistrial was declared.

Industry observers note that in June 2025, at her second trial, Read was acquitted of second-degree murder and the two lesser charges against her. Instead, Read was convicted of driving while under the influence and sentenced to one year of probation due to having no previous criminal convictions.

Since her second trial, Read has kept a relatively low profile, but she has not stayed out of the legal system altogether. She sued Massachusetts State Police and the town of Canton for negligence and civil conspiracy, arguing that they were biased in their investigation. Read was later awarded $100,000 by the Massachusetts State Police, which agreed to settle her lawsuit.

In a recent development, charles Melton has long loved substantial, baggy pants. Back in 2024, the actor landed on GQ’s annual list of best pants thanks to one extremely voluminous pair from the Japanese label Sillage. And if his fits this fall are any indication, Melton won’t be stepping away from the assertively wide bottoms anytime soon. In fact, he keeps wearing one fantastically huge pair after another.

The Her Private Hell star’s latest giant-trouser run kicked off in mid-October at the star-studded Academy Gala in Los Angeles. While A-list dressers like A$AP Rocky and Jacob Elordi showed up in respectfully roomy pants, Melton upped the ante in an ERL tuxedo that left no doubt about his dedication to the slouch. His cropped-front tailcoat was neat as a pin and fit like a glove, but his slacks were dramatically roomy and artfully rumpled—parachute pants gone black tie.

According to recent reports, later that same month, he popped up in Texas for the F1 Grand Prix in a very Fashion Dude outfit: Louis Vuitton workwear jacket, sporty sunglasses, bucket hat, and some choice Wales Bonner x Adidas Sambas. And on his legs? A twisted-seam silhouette billowy enough to make a scrum of downtown stylists and creative directors blush. ​.

But Melton saved his biggest look of all for last week in Fresh York. At a VIP dinner for the South Korean eyewear label Gentle Monster, he donned a matching set from Viviano, the Tokyo-based label from designer Viviano Sue. Cut from gabardine as dark as a moonless night, both his Harrington jacket and balloon trousers looked as though they’d been blown up to the size of a weather balloon and then deflated, leaving behind all the crinkles and creases. He contrasted the dramatic ensemble with a pair of tiny oval sunglasses, which capped the whole thing off just right.

Industry observers note that even as menswear’s ideal pant fit moves towards a relaxed straight leg, some guys who dove deep into the baggy waters aren’t quite ready to give their roomy fits up just yet. Melton clearly loves the look and wears it well. And when your gigantic trousers help you stand out in a crowd as effortlessly and stylishly as his do, why bother changing?

The best men's cashmere sweaters are a lot like that guy Bryce from high school. Remember him? The one who was valedictorian and the star quarterback and the lead in the musical, and still always really nice to you. Hell, he probably also volunteered on weekends. Well, the best men's cashmere sweaters are the Bryce of autumnal staples.

Industry observers note that cashmere is the strongest and warmest and softest and swankiest form of wool there is, and it’s here to take your dreary cold weather wardrobe to bold new heights of handsomeness and coziness. The very best cashmere sweaters instantly make whatever you happen to have on that day—a T-shirt and denim, say, or a button-down and blazer—look miles more considered, sophisticated, and polished.

Make sense? Good, because now comes the fun part: settling on the right cashmere sweater for you. Are you after a basic cashmere pullover? A svelte cashmere turtleneck, perhaps? How about a currently-trending cashmere cardigan? To help make that decision as simple and streamlined as possible, we found 16 of the very best men's cashmere sweaters on the planet—from the gigantic flexes worth dropping a paycheck on to the budget-friendly crewnecks you should cop in every color. You'll look even better than Bryce did the night he was crowned prom king. Take that, Bryce.

In 2025, Banana Republic hawks no shortage of discreet office-ready staples, but tucked in amongst them is one of the best cashmere sweater propositions you'll find today. Essentially, this is the platonic ideal of an affordable cashmere sweater: Soft as anything, snug at the wrists and hem, and still roomy enough in the body and shoulders.

But the folks at Banana Republic didn't down tools once they'd nailed the fit and fabric. (And that's exactly why they've earned the top spot in our rankings.) Instead, they paid a ton of attention to their color choices, turning out a range of dignified, unexpected, and expensive-feeling shades, from the dusty blue above to a spotted brown, reddish pink, and classy ecru—alongside your typical black, gray, and navy. No wonder 205 happy customers took the time to give it a five-star online review.

It has been revealed that after its supreme softness, cashmere’s best-known attribute is its high price. But thanks to the forces that be (globalization, capitalism, etc.) cashmere is shedding its high-falutin’ price tags. The quality of more affordable cashmere sweaters aren’t up to par with the truly nice stuff, of course, but some options are better than others.

For us, the best of the budget bunch is Uniqlo. For just a hundred bucks, you get a satisfyingly soft pure cashmere sweater in a classic, relaxed fit, available in an impressively wide range of colors. If you want an upgrade from merino wool without the massive price jump, Uniqlo’s your best bet. The style is timeless and the cashmere is softer than you’d expect for the pricepoint.

We’ve mentioned it time and time again: long-sleeve polos make you hot. And in winter, the best long-sleeve polos are made from luscious cashmere. And have the right fit. And a really good drape. And also a collar that’s not too small nor too thin.

All of that is usually one spinning plate too many for most brands, but Buck Mason is the Cirque du Soleil of knitwear and its California Cashmere Polo sweater is its harrowing act. The fabric is a 12-gauge jersey knit made from long-staple cashmere that has a pillowy hand and an elegant drape that, unlike many flimsy cashmeres, has plenty of structure. The neck hits the bullseye and is deep enough for a tee to peek out, but not so deep to reveal the insane graphic on noted tee. It also hits that middle-tier price point oh so well, and even out-classes some higher-priced options.

You don’t have to do much to a cashmere sweater for it to make a significant impression. The fabric itself speaks volumes, so even the most basic of knitwear options can instantly make an outfit feel a bit luxer, more considered, and altogether elevated. (Just think about how put together guys like David Beckham and Daniel Day-Lewis look wearing plain ol' pullovers.).

At the same time, though, a little visual flourish never hurt anybody, which is why we love these cashmere crewneck sweaters from the new J.Crew. They still let the cashmere do the talking, but the classic cable knit gives it a bit of visual interest and keeps it from falling flat. The quality cashmere is more than solid for the price and looks great solo with jeans and sneakers, but cleans up real good with a button-up peaking out and a blazer over top.

Recent findings suggest that there isn't too much to say here: You're either a cashmere hoodie person or you aren't. The ones who are, though, would tell you they make flights (and movie nights on the couch) a cosy, incognito dream, and allow you to get away with wearing a hoodie all kinds of other places that they wouldn't typically be welcome. And when it comes to where to find one, Todd Snyder is here, as always, with a handsome, clean silhouette that makes the cashmere hoodie's refined nature even more so. It also comes in three nice colours. Thanks Todd.

Industry observers note that most cashmere stuff feels very East Coast prep—all straight-laced and solid-colored—which makes sense, because the East Coast is where it’s cold. Back in 2007, though, LA designer Greg Chait flipped that on its head: under the moniker The Elder Statesman, he started making cashmere blankets, then sweaters and ponchos and socks and stuffed animals, with a distinctly Californian vibe.

According to recent reports, the stuff is often tie-dyed and dip-dyed, sometimes emblazoned with palm trees or magic mushrooms or the checkerboard pattern on your trusty Vans for a jolt of Justin-Bieber-exiting-Sushi-Park swagger. But here, Chait and co. are playing the hits, rendering their cult-favorite sweaters in six different straight-forward, appealing colors.

Working on an Irish isle, Inis Meáin has woven traditional Aran craftsmanship with modern techniques for decades. But, crucially, it still only produces its knits in small batches. Which means this is a rare, rare waffle.

According to recent reports, quince makes one of the best affordable cashmere sweaters on the market. It’s hard to disagree with the idea that a good piece of knitwear shouldn’t equate to a down payment on a home. It might not be as luxe as some of our other favorite options, but it’s still ultra soft, which means you can swaddle yourself comfortably without worrying about the damage this sweater has done to your bank account.

Whoever this supposed “Jordan” guy is, we’re guessing that Alex Mill named its cashmere sweater after the famed basketball legend because it also has it all: thick-gauge yarns, a fluffy texture, elegant drape, classic fit, and a perfect crew neck collar.

While some DTC cashmere brands focus solely on finding the luxest fibers, Everlane remains focused on its pricing also. The cashmere crewnecks use a blend of new cashmere and recycled cashmere for a reduced environmental impact, and still feel incredibly soft in the hand.

It has been revealed that mr P.—Mr Porter's in-house line—normally makes excellent, quiet basics. We're proud of the fictional man's decision to go off a little here.

According to recent reports, ghiaia Cashmere’s has expanded over the last few years but the brands initial focus is quite literally in the name. If there’s one place you can turn to when you’re in search of beautiful cashmere knits, then it’s Ghiaia. It’s knitted in Italy, and it has raglan sleeves with subtle ribbing in the sleeves and neck.

It has been revealed that the cardigan du jour is not the tight-fitting knit of trends gone by, but rather a thicker, looser variety. In fact, it's sort of looks just like this.

It has been revealed that extreme Cashmere's designs come in only one, inclusive size, so if you're a small person who likes a close fit—move on. But if you're anything else, swaddle thyself.

A deep cut from our Italian friends across the Atlantic, Fedeli is the go-to cashmere brand for many exacting Europeans.

Another polo sweater here, but this time from the luxury gods at Connolly.

Cashmere is a kind of wool that’s made from the undercoats of goats. While goat’s outercoats are thick and coarse to protect them from the harsher elements, the undercoat remains ultra soft and fine. The fibers are actually hollow which makes them great for insulation which is why cashmere is known for its super smooth hand and high warmth to weight ratio. What separates cashmere from other types of wool is its superior silky hand and fine fibers which can vary between 14 to 19 microns in thickness—thinner than even the finest sheep’s wool. For reference, human hairs are only as fine as about 50 microns.

Here's the catch: high-quality cashmere will usually cost you a pretty penny. For the price, you should be getting a form of cashmere made from long staple fibers spun into multi-ply yarns and knit into a tightly-tensioned fabric. Those factors all contribute to cashmere's pedigreed reputation as a material that's much less prone to pilling and stretching than its woolier counterparts. (That reputation, rightful or not, also informs its notoriously high price tag.) Cashmere is graded by its thickness and staple length with Grade A being the highest quality, followed by grades B and C. The higher the grade, the softer the yarns, the warmer the fabric, the better the durability.

Over the last few years, demand for good quality affordable cashmere sweaters has transformed the erstwhile rich-guy signifier into a bona fide cold weather staple you don't have to drain a 401(k) to afford. With one small caveat: supply chain transparency is infamously hard to suss out in the fashion industry, but don't expect a $100 cashmere joint—no matter how tony its source of origin—to hold up as well as a $500 one.

GQ Recommends heavily emphasizes our own editorial experience with those brands, how they make their clothes, and how those clothes have been reviewed by customers. Bottom line: GQ wouldn’t tell you to wear it if we wouldn’t.

We make every effort to cast as wide of a net as possible, with an eye on identifying the best options across three key categories: quality, fit, and price.

According to recent reports, to kick off the process, we enlist the GQ Recommends braintrust to vote on our contenders. Some of the folks involved have worked in retail, slinging clothes to the masses; others have toiled for small-batch menswear labels; all spend way too much time thinking about what hangs in their closets.

Across the majority of our buying guides, our team boasts firsthand experience with the bulk of our selects, but a handful are totally new to us. So after several months of intense debate, we tally the votes, collate the anecdotal evidence, and emerge with a list of what we believe to be the absolute best of the category right now, from the tried-and-true stalwarts to the modern disruptors, the affordable beaters to the wildly expensive (but wildly worth-it) designer riffs.

The Exact Order You Should Apply Your Skincare, According to Dermatologists

📅 04 Dec 2018 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3171 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love.
  • It has been revealed that the world of skincare can quickly become confusing and overwhelming.
  • Well, it’s time to stop mindlessly scrolling and start reading because team Cosmo tapped experts to break down the ideal skincare routine order that’s streamlined and effective for your exact concerns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

It has been revealed that the world of skincare can quickly become confusing and overwhelming. Doom-scrolling through SkinTok makes things seem even more complicated. Like, how many steps do you actually need? Which serums are worth using? What products are totally superfluous? If you followed every bit of “foolproof” advice you found on the app, your skin barrier would be compromised and your complexion could look worse than before you went down this rabbit hole.

Well, it’s time to stop mindlessly scrolling and start reading because team Cosmo tapped experts to break down the ideal skincare routine order that’s streamlined and effective for your exact concerns.

Trust us, it's a lot to consider even for beauty editors who spend their entire day testing all of these products, let alone a beginner just trying to get glowy, clear skin or deter fine lines. But step by step, we're gonna make sense of it all, below.

First things first: You do not need a 10-step skincare routine (or even a 5-step routine!). "Less is more when it comes to your skin—I'm all about product reducing," says dermatologist Karan Lal, MD. "In reality, our skin chemistry needs hydration and moisture to maintain a good skin barrier, which you can get from just a few products." And, as virtually all dermatologists agree, those products include the following:.

Recent findings suggest that that's it. The three most crucial skincare products are cleanser, moisturizer, and SPF. It’s not glamorous, but good skin doesn’t need to be (just ask your dermatologist or anyone on the Cosmo beauty team—simple is always better). The more products you layer on, the higher your risk is for irritation, allergic reactions, and breakouts, notes Dr. Lal.

Now, if you're looking to build a slightly more advanced skincare routine, we're totally on board with that, too. Keep reading to learn how to incorporate more skincare steps, and what order they should be applied.

“The rule of thumb when applying skincare is to apply the lightest formula first and the heaviest last since thinner products can’t penetrate thicker products,” states dermatologist Shereene Idriss, MD. Example: Layering a serum (thin) on top of your moisturizer (thick) would render that serum almost ineffective because it can't absorb into your skin when there's an occlusive barrier sitting on top of it.

Please, for the love of the beauty gods, remove your makeup and wash your face before slathering on your skincare products. “For ingredients to absorb properly, you need clean skin that’s totally free of oil and grime,” claims dermatologist Mona Gohara, MD, which is where double-cleansing comes in.

Sources indicate that wondering how to double cleanse? The simplest method is to remove your makeup with a cleansing oil or balm (neither is "better" than the other; it's just personal preference). This step will dissolve all the makeup on your face without stripping your skin.

Then, follow that up with a gentle cleanser that works with your skin type. Dry skin should look for creamy, non-foaming face washes with barrier-boosting ingredients like ceramides, hyaluronic acid, and glycerin; while oily skin should try gel-based face washes or gentle foaming cleansers.

Those with acne-prone skin will benefit from a formula with added acne-fighting ingredients, like salicylic acid or benzoyl peroxide. Keep in mind, though: If your skin is sensitive, use soothing formulas loaded with things like colloidal oatmeal, aloe vera, and niacinamide.

It depends, but usually yes. If you have oily or acne-prone skin, then definitely yes—cleansing after you wake up is a good way to get rid of any grime or shine that's collected overnight. However, if you have dry or sensitive skin, you probs don't need to re-wash ahead of the rest of your routine, but if you're a sweaty sleeper, it's always a good idea to freshen your face before the rest of your skincare routine.

Face toners used to be terrible, alcohol-based liquids that burned your face. But today’s (good) toners are either filled with gentle, hydrating ingredients for dry and sensitive skin, or filled with chemical exfoliants to treat acne and bumps. “Toners are not meant to be something that sits around on your skin and feels heavy,” indicates Dr. Gohara. “They’re just priming your face for ingredients to be better absorbed later on.”.

Reminder: Toner (like most of the steps on this list) is optional, but if your toner smells like nail polish remover or alcohol, you need to ditch it—fast—and find an updated version instead. The best toner for acne-prone or oily skin is gonna be filled with ingredients that'll help unclog pores and prevent breakouts, like salicylic acid and/or AHAs. Tap it on your skin every other night (or morning, if you initiative to use a retinol at night), then wait 60 seconds before layering another product.

If your skin is dry and/or sensitive, choose a toner with hydrating ingredients to reduce potential irritation (like hyaluronic acid, polyglutamic acid, squalane, ceramides, etc.). You can pat this onto your skin every morning, night, or both.

Sources indicate that toners and essences are pretty interchangeable in their consistencies, so if you’re looking for when to use your essence in your skincare routine, use it as step 2 (instead of toner). If you happen to have both in your routine, swipe on a toner first, then pat in an essence. (Think of it like a thin moisturizer-serum hybrid.).

Exfoliators keep skin smooth and clear by removing built-up dead skin cells and excess oil that can dull your complexion and block product absorption. They should be used after toner, when the skin is clean and balanced, and before serums so your treatments can penetrate more effectively.

Recent findings suggest that there are two types of exfoliators: Chemical and physical. Chemical exfoliants use acids or enzymes (like AHAs, BHAs, or PHAs) to dissolve dead skin cells and are best for concerns like acne, clogged pores, uneven texture, and dark spots. Physical exfoliants use gentle scrubbing particles to manually buff skin smooth and can give instant results, but should be used carefully to avoid irritation.

Industry observers note that incorporate an exfoliator into your routine one to three times per week for ongoing skin concerns, especially if you have sensitive or acne-prone skin. Don’t forget to follow exfoliation with hydrating products and sunscreen during the day, too!

In a recent development, “Serums are essentially shots of extremely concentrated nutrients, hydrators, or antioxidants that really amp up your skin health as soon as you apply them,” claims Dr. Gohara. “People often skip out on using them, but they’re honestly the heavy lifters of your skincare routine.” So, while serums are totally optional, they’re often a good first step to leveling up your skincare routine and boosting your skin health.

For almost all skin types, Dr. Gohara, Dr. Lal, Dr. Idriss, and every other derm in existence, swear by using a vitamin C serum in the morning, which protects your skin from inflammation and damage caused by environmental factors, while also brightening dark spots over time. Just note: Vitamin C can be strong, so if your skin is sensitive, use it every other morning (or every two mornings) instead.

Though serums are optional, all skin types can benefit from using a hydrating, hyaluronic-acid-based serum at night (and, honestly, in the morning too), which pulls water into your skin from the air to keep it hydrated. “If you’re using acne treatments or anti-aging products—which can be drying or irritating—you want to prep your skin with as much moisture as possible first,” claims Dr. Idriss.

Totally. But when it comes to layering serums, keep in mind the thin-to-thick rule, says dermatologist Jessie Cheung, MD. "Thicker serums may impede the absorption of the thinner formulations," she notes. So you'll want to start with your watery, vitamin C serums, then layer on rich, creamy formulas after.

It has been revealed that eye creams tend to be lighter and thinner than face moisturizers, so make sure to apply them before your creams and oils if you opt to use one. (Remember: lighter products go before heavier products).

Recent findings suggest that for morning use, look for an eye cream that's packed with caffeine, which helps temporarily constrict and tighten puffy under-eyes within 20 minutes. And, ideally, opt for one with a cooling applicator; “the cold steel helps with fluid retention—aka under-eye bags—especially if you keep the cream in the fridge between uses,” claims Dr. Gohara.

It has been revealed that “Most people think a night eye cream should contain retinol to help with fine lines, but in reality, you want to be gentle," indicates Dr. Gohara. "Your eye area is delicate and at risk for irritation, so tap on a simple, hydrating eye cream that’ll protect your under-eyes and repair your skin barrier overnight.”.

It has been revealed that ideally, spot treatments are best applied at night (whether they’re for zits, scars, or dark spots), because that’s when your body is working hardest to repair itself, notes Dr. Gohara. But if your nighttime routine already includes acids or retinoids, try spot-treating in the morning, so you don’t irritate your skin with too much at once.

According to recent reports, regardless of when you apply your spot treatment, make sure to tap it on before your moisturizer so it can really penetrate your skin and do the most without having another barrier to penetrate (before?! What?! Yes, just trust the process and keep reading).

Sources indicate that for scars: Dr. Idriss recommends using a spot treatment with either hydroquinone (a skin-bleaching ingredient that works fast but can be highly irritating) or niacinamide (aka vitamin B3), which gently brightens marks and scars over time. Niacinamide can be used daily (most formulas won’t cause irritation), but hydroquinone should be used once every three days to be safe (zero irritation after two weeks? Move it up to every other day).

For acne: Dr. Gohara stands by tried-and-true benzoyl peroxide and salicylic acid—but not together, unless you want to dry out or irritate your skin. Benzoyl peroxide kills acne-causing bacteria (use it for classic whiteheads), while salicylic acid dissolves oil and skin cells (use it for little clogged pores and inflamed bumps).

How to use spot treatments:Regardless of which formula you choose, the application is the same: Dab a thin layer over your spot or zit and wait a full minute for it to dry. Then, to prevent the treatment from getting wiped around your face, apply your moisturizer to the rest of your face, avoiding the spots. When your face is fully moisturized, tap a dot of moisturizer on top of the spot treatment.

Recent findings suggest that you should stick on a pimple patch (which, FYI, is a sticker that help protect your pimple, soak up any excess fluid or oil around it, and potentially help treat your zit depending on if it has added actives like salicylic acid) before moisturizer, just as you would with other spot treatments. Typically, I will stick on a pimple patch, then carefully spread my moisturizer across my face to avoid moving the patch around.

"You need to be using a moisturizer twice a day," claims Dr. Lal. "Your skin barrier requires moisture and hydration to stay healthy," he adds, noting that all skin types should load up on formulas rich in ceramides, glycerin, and hyaluronic acid. “A moisturizer also helps trap in all the products underneath it to make the ingredients even more effective," adds Dr. Idriss.

In a recent development, you can use the same moisturizer morning and night, FYI. But some might prefer a lighter-weight option in the morning, or one that combines SPF for a lil two-in-one action. Oily skin should look for lightweight moisturizers in a gel-based formula to keep skin hydrated without feeling greasy.

The best dry-skin moisturizers “should be filled with all the things your body naturally produces and can use more of, like hyaluronic acid, lipids, and proteins,” says Dr. Gohara. Cream-based formulas will be your BFF, morning and night.

If you want, you can tiptoe into the retinol game by using an anti-aging night cream in the p.m., which usually has a gentler, “watered-down” dose of retinoids. That being noted, it’s often easier—and less irritating—to use your regular moisturizer and layer a retinol on top (see: the next step).

“Retinoids—the general term for all vitamin-A derivatives, including retinol—sink into your skin to speed up cell turnover, causing your body to churn out fresher, smoother, less-wrinkled skin over time,” says Dr. Gohara. Remember that retinoids take four to six months of consistent use to give you results, so using it every day is key.

In a recent development, but just because it might take half a year to see your wrinkles smooth out doesn’t mean you won’t see more immediate results in other ways. “Retinoids trigger collagen production and cellular exfoliation,” adds Dr. Gohara, “which means they’ll also fade dark spots, smooth scars, clear pores, prevent breakouts, and brighten skin.” Basically, retinoids are the best multitasking product dermatologists recommend.

It has been revealed that all retinoids aren't created equal. In order of most powerful to least, it starts with prescription-strength retinoids (like tretinoin), adapalene (which is prescription-strength but sold over-the-counter), retinal (or retinaldehyde), and then retinol. There are also a ton of over-the-counter derivatives of vitamin A in addition to retinal and retinol.

The more sensitive or dry your skin, the weaker your retinoid should be. That, or you'll need a longer acclimation period to get used to it (more on that in a sec). You can also find over-the-counter retinoids paired with anti-inflammatory ingredients, such as niacinamide, to offset their side effects.

If you’re newly introduced to retinoids, make sure to start slow to mitigate the initial adjustment period of flakes and sensitivity. “Apply a pea-size drop to your entire face one night a week for one week, then two nights a week for two weeks, then three nights a week for three weeks, and then every other night indefinitely,” indicates Dr. Gohara.

And if you do have extra-sensitive skin, apply a layer of moisturizer 10 minutes before and 10 minutes after your retinol to reduce irritation without totally diluting the treatment. Think of it like sandwiching your face in moisture.

It has been revealed that if you’re already using (or planning to use) a night cream with retinoids, doubling up won’t make the anti-aging results more effective—it’ll just cause inflammation. And if you're pregnant or breastfeeding, retinol is also off-limits.

Sunscreen (of at least SPF 30+) is the absolute last step—and perhaps the most key. “Sunscreen is there to protect your face and act as armor against the outside world,” states Dr. Gohara. “Basically, it’s not adding anything to your skin—it’s protecting your skin.”.

And before you tell yourself that the SPF 15 in your foundation is good enough, know this: “The absolute bare minimum SPF you need on your face is SPF 30,” says Dr. Gohara. Unless you’re cool with premature aging, worsened acne scars, and an increased cancer risk.

Sunscreens come in a ton of different formulations nowadays. No more of the gloopy, uncomfortable SPFs from childhood! If you have oily or acne-prone skin, for instance, you might prefer sunscreen with chemical filters, since these feel lightweight on skin and sink in quickly. If your skin is dry, look for a formula with hyaluronic acid or ceramides, as these help skin retain moisture as you wear it.

Recent findings suggest that if you're prone to sensitivities, reach for a mineral-based sunscreen. These use either titanium dioxide, zinc oxide, or both to sit on skin and shield UVA and UVB rays—and, since they don't actually penetrate skin, tend to be less likely to cause reactions than their chemical counterparts. Otherwise, go with a formula that you'll be comfortable slathering on every! single! day!

After all, "sunscreen not only reduces your risk of skin cancer, but it also prevents the formation of abnormal collagen and elastin," says Dr. Lal. Basically, a layer of sunscreen today helps prevent 65-year-old you from having thick, mottled, leathery skin.

It has been revealed that again, "the best sunscreen is the one you'll actually use every day," says Dr. Lal. But your skin will look and feel its best with two separate products. "Moisturizers formulated with sunscreen can be more sensitizing and won't have as many moisturizing benefits," he says. So, like, it's better than nothing, but it's not ideal.

According to recent reports, the order of your skincare routine, as well as how and when you apply your skincare products, can make a huge difference in your results. Think about it: If you apply a lightweight serum on top of a rich moisturizer, you're likely not going to experience much from that serum, since it can't penetrate into your skin. But this specific order also can help avoid potential skin irritations and breakouts, like when combining ingredients that can't be used together (i.e., retinol and vitamin C).

Sources indicate that you can start a skincare routine at any age. In fact, the sooner you start, the better, indicates dermatologist Dr. Cheung. "You’re never too young to start protecting your skin," she notes. If you're a beginner, start with the above routine (cleanser, moisturizer, SPF—the holy trinity, IMO), and slowly add additional products depending on what your skin needs.

“You can’t fuck with Keith Richards.” That’s what Sam Houser told me when I asked the inspiration for his company name, Rockstar Games. “I’m a huge fan of the classic golden era of rock stars—both the music, but also the life,” he went on. “You can't argue with Keith Moon riding in a Rolls Royce with a blowup doll hanging out the back and a woman in there screaming, ‘I'm being raped.’ The guy is the original punk rocker. And if we can bring a fraction of that to games, then we’re doing something.”.

It has been revealed that it was October 2002, just a few weeks before the release of their latest blockbuster, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. I’d come to their glossy loft in Soho, Manhattan to interview the elusive 30-year-old Houser and Rockstar co-founders, his younger brother Dan Houser and managing director Terry Donovan, for Rolling Stone. It would be one of their first, last and only in-depth sit-downs together before they decided that the world’s most successful and controversial video game required little explanation from them at all.

Recent findings suggest that I continued reporting on them and their games during the raucous and turbulent years to follow: hitting over $10 billion in sales, getting compared to Balzac and Dickens in Time magazine, being sued (unsuccessfully) for causing real-life violence. As I investigated in my book Jacked: The Outlaw Story of Grand Theft Auto, they also triggered what remains the most outrageous and cinematic scandal ever to hit the industry: the discovery of a hidden sex scene in 2005’s GTA San Andreas that would inspire attempts to legislate and ban the game. As Hilary Clinton remarked at the time, “The disturbing material in Grand Theft Auto and other games like it is stealing the innocence of our children and it’s making the difficult job of being a parent even harder.”.

With the gamer generation now grown up and in power, the Reefer Madness panic around GTA has finally given way to something more crucial: this little game out of Scotland has become the most successful and influential entertainment product of all time. Today, Rockstar returns to Vice City with the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. More than a decade in the making, with a budget Rockstar has never disclosed but analysts put between $1 billion and $2 billion, the game follows Jason Duval, an ex-soldier, and Lucia Caminos, who phones him from prison, as they’re pulled into a criminal conspiracy across a send-up of Miami. Its first trailer has been viewed more than 300 million times on YouTube, and footage premiering on Netflix nearly crashed the streamer’s servers. Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar’s parent organization, expects record revenue of $8.1 billion this fiscal year.

Sources indicate that for longtime fans, GTA 6 marks something more personal: the first game in the franchise since the original band behind it broke up. Following the departure of Donovan and other central figures, Dan Houser exited Rockstar in 2020, leaving his substantial brother Sam as the last founder still there. With Sam remaining notoriously quiet about the new game, I went digging through my old tapes and found my long-lost interview with gaming’s original punk rockers. During our two-hour talk, the young co-founders were brash, unrepentant, and championing a lifetime of obsessions, as Sam put it. “I wasn’t just obsessed about games,” he told me, “we were obsessed about everything—obsessive about music, obsessive about film, obsessive about fashion.”.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 demonstrates that the obsession never left him. Here in this exclusive excerpt from my interview, the Rockstars share how it all started.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that when Newly introduced York City mayor Zohran Mamdani passed out water bottles to marathoners on Nov.
  • If it feels like no one’s talked about Movember for a while, that’s because the non-profit charity’s heyday online peaked in 2012.
