#146152. Western Brands Need a Upcoming China Playbook

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2318 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vogue ↗ Open Full Page

Western Brands Need a Upcoming China Playbook

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2318 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Western luxury in China has hit serious roadblocks in recent years.
  • “I think the relationship between Chinese consumers and Western brands is undergoing a significant shift,” says Cherry Xu, founder of Shanghai-based fashion-art foundation Cheruby.
  • It has been revealed that the latest round of earnings revealed that China’s luxury market is taking longer to stabilize than hoped.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Western luxury in China has hit serious roadblocks in recent years. The old approach of opening stores and investing in top-down marketing is now ineffective, as local consumers look elsewhere for authenticity and clear value propositions. And so, the brands that rise to the challenge by localizing their output, optimizing distribution, and adapting to China’s fresh consumer will be best placed when the market recovers.

“I think the relationship between Chinese consumers and Western brands is undergoing a significant shift,” says Cherry Xu, founder of Shanghai-based fashion-art foundation Cheruby. “Younger generations no longer automatically associate Western origins or heritage with greater value.”.

It has been revealed that the latest round of earnings revealed that China’s luxury market is taking longer to stabilize than hoped. According to Bain’s report released early this year, the mainland Chinese personal luxury market contracted 3-5% in 2025. And although it displayed signs of recovery in the second half of the year, fashion, specifically, is still struggling. “There have been quite a few [Chinese] store closures, and I think the mood is unsupportive of luxury,” Goldman Sachs luxury analyst Erwan Rambourg told Vogue Business in October.

“The third quarter brought a more challenging Chinese consumer backdrop with a ‘feel-good’ factor deteriorating at the very beginning of the quarter,” LVMH CFO Cécile Cabanis noted during the group’s earnings call in October. Until June, Hermès was growing in Greater China, but is now broadly flat year-on-year following the Q3 results due to a decline in traffic. Kering declined 8% in the Asia-Pacific region, excluding Japan. CEO Luca de Meo said in a statement that “delivering our action proposal in China” will help the group to restore momentum. At Prada Group, too, China remained a weak point.

“Weaker consumer confidence, slower economic growth, and heightened price sensitivity are weighing on discretionary spending, following more than a decade in which China was a key driver of global luxury growth,” said Fflur Roberts, head of luxury goods at Euromonitor International.

In recent years, domestic brands have shone in China by embracing their native understanding of Chinese cultural sensibilities and offering better value for money, as consumers show heightened price sensitivity — a substantial drag on the discretionary spending that once drove major growth for global luxury players. Local brands are especially well placed to adapt to the rising “Guochao” (direct translation: “national tide”) movement, which incorporates traditional Chinese style elements into contemporary styles.

According to recent reports, chinese luxury consumers continue to engage with Chanel, despite a sluggish market. Pictured: Shan Yichun.

Additionally, Western luxury brands must increasingly compete with a shift in China’s premium consumption. China International Capital Corporation’s (CICC) vice president Liwei Hou reports that overall tenant sales at Chinese high-end malls outperformed luxury brand growth in 2025 and 2026. “Sportswear (Arc’teryx, Salomon) and affordable brands (like Ralph Lauren), as well as Chinese brands (Laopu, Songmont), and fine dining have been the star performers in these high-end malls,” she says. “A crisis of luxury is an opportunity for others. Proactive changes are needed.”.

Until Western brands audit their approach — a time-consuming and complex process — domestic Chinese brands may continue to capture market share, analysts agree, capitalizing on the cost-effective manufacturing infrastructure at their fingertips, which makes room for bigger margins.

It has been revealed that for starters, Western brands must adapt to the leading consumer. Experts agree that the commercial backbone for luxury brands in China is the established millennial and Gen X clients, particularly for bigger-ticket purchases.

In a recent development, in Bain’s 2025 report on China’s personal luxury goods market, the firm found that consumer motivations for buying luxury had shifted away from signaling status to a more refined appreciation and discernment. “The Chinese consumer hasn’t stopped spending. They’ve stopped overpaying for a logo. Status has moved from visible wealth to taste, craft, and wellbeing,” states Jonathan Travers-Smith, CEO of Hotpot, an agency bringing Western brands into East Asian markets. Brands must demonstrate real craft, a credible story and prices that feel earned, Travers-Smith advises. “Some Western houses have priced their way out of that conversation, raising prices year after year while the in-store experience stayed the same.” In addition, he argues, brands should halt price hikes and invest in clienteling.

“The industry has spent a lot of time talking about creativity and marketing, but I think the bigger challenge is rebuilding a sense of value,” indicates Thomas Chauvet, Citi’s head of luxury goods research. Simply lowering prices is not the answer, he believes. Rather, brands must develop stronger products, better assortments, greater differentiation, and a clearer reason for consumers to buy.

Industry observers note that burberry’s approach to China is working well, confirmed CEO Joshua Schulman on the investor call earlier this month. Greater China’s retail growth grew (5%) in Q2 of fiscal 2026, carried by local spending. This followed a 9% climb in Q1. “We clearly understand that the market in China is challenging right now,” mentioned Schulman. “That said, we are pleased with our outperformance in a dynamic market. And this has been going on for several quarters.” The brand, he revealed, had risen to the challenge over the last two years, aligning pricing with consumer expectations — aware that globally, and in China especially, consumers were fatigued by exorbitant price points. “This was a historic positioning that we had,” said Schulman. “And coming back to this sweet spot in the luxury market has been a priority for us. We see that this is resonating strongly with our Chinese consumers.”.

Industry observers note that the Western brands that are performing have renewed desire through fresh ideas, centered on experiences, travel, beauty and wellness, not just novelty for novelty’s sake. “Creative leadership is central to this process. Matthieu Blazy’s appointment at Chanel offers an example of how a latest creative direction can introduce a fresh perspective to an established house and generate renewed consumer interest,” indicates Julio Ng, co-founder of brand development consultancy 2034. It’s understood that Chanel is performing well in China, despite the downturn for other players.

Recent findings suggest that ralph Lauren is another outlier. Brand CEO Patrice Louvet told investors earlier this month that China sales remained strong in Q2, increasing more than 35%, bolstered by store sales as well as distribution expansion. Its output remains rooted in premium American style that’s more affordable than most luxury players, resonating with value-conscious Chinese consumers.

“What Chanel and Ralph Lauren do particularly well is that they both have a very distinct sense of world-building,” says Xu. “Chanel has established a cultural presence beyond fashion through art, cinema, and creative expression, while Ralph Lauren offers an entire lifestyle and aesthetic universe.” She argues that both remain true to their identities while creating different entry points into their worlds, noting that brands wanting to build lasting brand value need a clear identity, compelling products, and a consistent creative vision.

Ralph Lauren grew China sales more than 35% in the last quarter. Pictured: Actor Kevin Chu.

Sources indicate that calvin Wang, a luxury and retail consultant, is dubbing it the shift to “rational indulgence”. He explains that VICs should be respected as connoisseurs. “Approach clients with the understanding that they often know more and have seen more than the brand’s frontline staff,” he indicates. Wang encourages a focus on UHNWIs to handle the K-shaped economy, where the top end of the economy grows, but the lower end lags as inequalities widen. However, he still recommends maintaining connections to upper-middle-class consumers by offering products of demonstrable quality and longevity.

“When it comes to what brands can control, I think that the focus has to be on reigniting product desirability, so investing in marketing and in innovative retail experience should be the priority,” says Carole Madjo, luxury goods analyst at Barclays.

Recent findings suggest that in the past, international brands have struggled to land a successful localization strategy in China, often oversimplifying the process. “A China strategy cannot simply be an adaptation of global marketing materials,” notes Olivia Chen, co-founder of Shanghai-based brand agency 2034. “Local teams need sufficient understanding of the brand, as well as the authority to make decisions that respond to the market. At the same time, local activity needs to remain aligned with the brand’s international positioning.” Chen sees it as a balancing act. If a Western brand becomes too localized, it loses the qualities that first made it attractive — that is, what the brand represents beyond China.

Sources indicate that “With the increasingly global circulation of information and culture, younger generations are developing their own sensibilities and identities at the intersection of global culture and local experience,” notes Xu. “Rather than approaching Chinese consumers as a distinctly separate audience, brands are engaging with individuals who have both a global cultural perspective and their own local experiences. I think this is changing the way we understand localization.”.

Burberry’s localization approach? “Combining our British luxury heritage with locally relevant product and storytelling,” said Schulman on the brand’s most recent investor call. “In the second quarter, we had capsule collections for Chinese Valentine’s Day, and we also had a localized activation with China National Geography. All of those show our appreciation for and understanding of the local customer.”.

Recent findings suggest that to this day, major brands still produce red-colored Lunar New Year collections. But they should “avoid superficial ‘Guochao’ tokenism,” warns Wang. “Designing literal Chinese-themed capsules — such as applying zodiac animals or traditional calligraphy onto Western silhouettes — frequently reads as opportunistic and patronizing. Chinese luxury consumers already look to domestic designers for authentic cultural expression.”.

Equally, brands must develop strong strategies beyond local celebrity endorsements and seasonal campaigns. Travers-Smith takes a hardline on this. “Listen before you spend. Go deep into Xiaohongshu and Douyin for insights into how consumers actually talk about your category, your product, and competitors,” he says. “Build one or two cultural moments a year that are made in China — not adapted for China.” He also encourages empowering an on-the-ground China digital team to make decisions, embrace faster content cycles, and cater content based on different market needs across cities.

For a Western luxury house, Burberry is outperforming in the China market thanks to effective localization. Pictured: Actor Wu Lei.

Travers-Smith pinpoints a substantial misconception that Chinese social media is a channel for pushing campaigns. The reality? “It’s where consumers decide what to buy, and Xiaohongshu is a search engine for taste. Building beautifully polished brand-owned content should be the second priority after ensuring your brand is communicated through UGC from influencers and key opinion leaders (KOLs).”.

As for product assortment and store networks, brands should streamline, Bismuth recommends. This means closing underperforming stores, moving away from promotional activity, and slowing down on retail expansion. This shift is already underway. Louis Vuitton, Dior, Loro Piana, and Tiffany opened new flagship stores in Tier-1 cities while scaling back presence in Tier-2 and Tier-3 locations over recent years. Nonetheless, some insiders favor a more selective approach over a blanket Tier-1-only strategy. One core takeaway experts agree on: treat China as a continent made up of several unique territories.

Recent findings suggest that western companies must also take stock of their wholesale and direct-to-consumer (DTC) networks. “Brands need people who understand their positioning and can represent them in a way that supports their long-term ambitions,” claims Chen. “China is a complex market to navigate, and a brand’s reputation can be affected by how and where its products are sold.”.

According to recent reports, the Chinese DTC landscape is fundamentally different from the rest of the world’s. Discovery, communication, and client relationships are built predominantly on platforms like WeChat’s mini-programs (sub-applications often used for e-commerce) and Tmall Luxury Pavilion (a premium e-concession platform). “Brands must focus on connecting and aligning the distinct strengths of each platform to create a seamless consumer journey,” states Wang.

It has been revealed that because of the macro downturn and the growing maturity of a relatively new major market, analysts struggle to outline a recovery timeline for Western luxury in China. One thing is clear: brands should not wait it out. “The slump might be cyclical, but the change in behavior is structural,” states Travers-Smith. “Property wealth isn’t coming back to 2021 levels, and the consumer who learned to buy less and better isn’t going to unlearn it.”.

The smartest players will address issues the boom hid and strategize for potential market disruptors. “For 2027, watch AI. Assistants like Doubao and Qwen are becoming the first place people ask what to buy,” warns Travers-Smith. “If your brand isn’t described accurately and favorably in those answers, you’re invisible at the moment of consideration.”.

According to recent reports, in the mid to long-term, luxury houses should also ramp up their knowledge and insights on Chinese Gen Z and Gen Alpha. “[They] are expected to become key pillars for businesses in 10-20 years, and it is never too early to start understanding them and interacting with them,” states Hou. Even today, the Gen Z contingent might not drive direct revenue, but they can give brands cultural relevance.

Recent findings suggest that china’s Gen Z isn’t a core consumer yet, but Western brands should continue to court the group. Pictured: Actor Wang Yibo.

“I would love to see more brands move beyond cultural marketing and towards cultural production. This could mean building long-term relationships with local artists, designers, and independent cultural institutions, supporting research, commissioning fresh work, and encouraging cross-disciplinary exchanges,” claims Xu. “These investments may take longer to develop, but they have the potential to create value for both the brand and the local cultural ecosystem.”.

For Western brands, waiting it out is not a viable option. It’s an expensive mistake. Chauvet encourages action: “Chinese luxury demand may recover, but I suspect the market that emerges will be more mature and more competitive than the one brands enjoyed over the past decade.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there are only so many dishes you can make in your oven on Thanksgiving, so we’ve made it easy for you with a no-bake stuffing that doesn’t require taking up oven space. Instead, we use a slow cooker that’ll help you whip up your stuffing alongside the stars of the show (roast turkey and pumpkin pie, obviously!). While you buzz around the kitchen, the slow cooker will cook your stuffing for you — resulting in a delicious Thanksgiving side dish waiting for you to serve up.

According to recent reports, arrange a rack in the center of the oven and preheat it to 350°. Spread bread on a baking sheet. Bake the bread, tossing it halfway through, until it is crispy and feels dry. The edges should just be starting to turn golden, which should take about 15 to 20 minutes. Meanwhile, melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. When melted, add celery, onion, and herbs. Season with salt and pepper and cook until the onions are translucent, about 7 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool.

Grease your Crock-Pot bowl and add the toasted bread. Pour the vegetable mixture, eggs, broth, and parsley over the bread. Toss to combine and cover.

Cook on low for 3 to 4 hours, stirring after 2 hours have passed. Garnish with parsley before serving.

The full list of ingredients and instructions can be found in the recipe below.

Thanksgiving is hectic, we get it. This is the perfect dish to set aside while you prepare everything else. After the 3 hour cook time, switch the pot to the "keep warm" setting—just give it a stir every 30 minutes or so to make sure the bread around the edges doesn't dry out. If the stuffing is ready hours before dinner time, you can add up to ¼ cup of broth every few hours to keep things hydrated.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, pumpkin pie bars are the easiest way to get the classic dessert on your Thanksgiving table. It requires no crust, chilling, or crimping. All you have to do is press it into the pan and your crust is ready to go! Way less time, way more glory. Sources indicate that NRCC Chairman Richard Hudson, right, here at a hearing in June, lost his reelection bid in North Carolina's 9th District. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

It has been revealed that north Carolina Rep. Richard Hudson, the chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee, has lost his race for reelection, a stinging defeat for the man charged with preserving the House majority for the GOP.

Hudson fell to Democrat Richard Ojeda, a former West Virginia state senator who was leading  51 percent to 49 percent Thursday afternoon  when The Associated Press called the race in North Carolina’s 9th District.

Hudson had already conceded the race Wednesday, when it became clear that his path to victory was closing off.

Sources indicate that “[The] voters of North Carolina’s 9th District made their choice and I respect it,” he said in a statement. “Since 2013 I’ve worked for North Carolina families. That includes the soldiers and families at Fort Bragg, who sacrifice more for this country than most people will ever know.”.

Hudson is now the second party campaign chief to lose his seat during a midterm election this decade. In 2022, New York Rep. Sean Patrick Maloney lost reelection while serving as chair of the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee.

Republicans across North Carolina experienced devastating losses on election night. As of Thursday afternoon, Democrats had also flipped the seats of Reps. Addison McDowell, Brad Knott and Tim Moore, as well as the open seat of retiring Rep. Chuck Edwards. The races for five other GOP-held seats remain uncalled, while Democratic Rep. Don Davis was reelected despite being targeted for defeat under a newly introduced GOP-drawn congressional map. Republicans also lost control of the North Carolina House and lost seats in the state Senate.

Recent findings suggest that north Carolina’s 9th District, which includes the Eastern Piedmont region and the Fayetteville area, was far from the House battlefield for much of the midterm cycle. President Donald Trump carried the seat by 16 points in 2024, according to calculations by Inside Elections with Nathan L. Gonzales, and Hudson won a seventh term the same year by nearly 19 points. Hudson also held a financial advantage over Ojeda, raising $4.2 million to Ojeda’s $2.9 million through mid-October.

But in the waning weeks of the campaign, signs of Republican concern grew and Hudson’s campaign began spending on ads.

In a recent development, ojeda was first elected to the West Virginia Senate in 2016. He ran for the U.S. House two years later as a Trump-voting Democrat but lost that race to Republican Carol Miller. He then briefly ran for the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination and also challenged GOP Sen. Shelley Moore Capito later that cycle but lost in the Democratic primary.

Ojeda moved to North Carolina in 2020, he told CityView, a local magazine, and he announced his challenge to Hudson last year.

Throughout the campaign, he attacked the incumbent over his support for Trump’s agenda, particularly the war in Iran. Ojeda is a retired Army major and the district is home to Fort Bragg, the nation’s largest Army base by population, where the Democrat was previously stationed for more than a decade.

“We did the impossible,’’ Ojeda told supporters Tuesday night. “We took on the chair of the National Republican Congressional Committee, a man with political connections, the billionaire donors, and the entire Washington establishment standing beside him.”.

Hudson, 55, is finishing his seventh term in the House and his second term as NRCC chair. He had no primary opponent this year and had grown used to winning reelection by comfortable margins.

Recent findings suggest that as a legislator, Hudson focused much of his policy agenda on health issues such as federal pandemic preparedness programs. He serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and chairs the panel's Communications and Technology Subcommittee.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mussels deserve your attention on weeknights. An affordable and accessible protein, they also happen to cook in less time than it takes to boil water. As the bivalves steam, they release a briny liquid, further perfuming the buttery, sake-fortified miso broth. Load up each bowl with a few good ladles, slurping every drop with an assist from crusty bread or warm rice. And why not enjoy the rest of the bottle of sake alongside your meal?

The seafood counter at your supermarket should sell rinsed and debarred mussels, but it’s easy to do at home. Discard any with cracked shells. Gently tap open raw mussels on a counter to see if they slowly close; if they do, those are okay to use. Swish them in a water-filled salad spinner or colander fitted inside a bowl, draining and refilling until water runs clear (give any especially dirty ones a scrub with a sponge). Use a towel to pull off the fibrous beard and set on a towel-lined tray in the fridge until you’re ready to cook.

More seafood dinners this way: Avgolemono Seafood Stew; Spaghetti alle Vongole; and Gorgeous Green Shrimp.

In a recent development, place 2 Tbsp. scallions from 8 scallions, thinly sliced on a diagonal, in a small bowl and set aside for serving.

Melt 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add 8 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and remaining scallions to pot and cook, stirring often, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add 2 Tbsp. white miso paste and ½ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes (if using) and cook until miso is broken up and incorporated into butter, about 20 seconds. Pour in 1 cup dry sake or dry white wine and stir to combine, then add 3–3½ lb. mussels, scrubbed, debearded. Cover pot and increase heat to medium-high. Cook, shaking pot occasionally, until mussels open, 5–7 minutes (discard any that do not open). Remove pot from heat.

Squeeze 1 lemon half over mussels. Cut remaining 1 lemon half into wedges for serving. Taste broth and season with kosher salt if needed.

Ladle mussels and broth among shallow bowls, then scatter reserved scallions over. Serve with country-style bread or steamed white rice if desired and lemon wedges for squeezing over.

#146145. Latest Update: Sheroanawe Hakihiiwe’s Tender Record of a Vanishing Amazon

Latest Update: Sheroanawe Hakihiiwe’s Tender Record of a Vanishing Amazon

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1187 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that to reach his home in Mahekoto, a Yanomami community deep in the Amazon, Sheroanawe Hakihiiwe, one of the most lauded Venezuelan artists working today, first flies from Caracas to the southern town of Puerto Ayacucho.
  • Recent findings suggest that the village, home to around 300 people, has no electricity and no phone signal.
  • For the past 30 years, Hakihiiwe has been devoted to making art about his homeland.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that to reach his home in Mahekoto, a Yanomami community deep in the Amazon, Sheroanawe Hakihiiwe, one of the most lauded Venezuelan artists working today, first flies from Caracas to the southern town of Puerto Ayacucho. From there, it’s an eight-day journey by boat along the Orinoco River.

Recent findings suggest that the village, home to around 300 people, has no electricity and no phone signal. Hakihiiwe spends his days in close communion with nature, fishing, hunting, and gathering. In a notebook, he draws everything he sees.

For the past 30 years, Hakihiiwe has been devoted to making art about his homeland. “I want to show both the grandeur of the rainforest and the quiet importance of something as delicate as an insect’s eyelash,” he claims. “Every element, no matter how small, contributes to that balance and the way life functions.”.

Recent findings suggest that we are speaking on the occasion of his first solo museum exhibition in the US, at the Institute of Contemporary Art, Miami (ICA Miami), in partnership with the Fondation Cartier pour l’art contemporain. On view through March 28, 2027, “Sheroanawe Hakihiiwe” brings together more than 100 works spanning his decades-long career, from his earliest experiments on handmade paper in the 1990s to breathtaking installations and a newly commissioned film shaped by his recent initiation as a shaman.

Sources indicate that for the show, Taller de Arquitectura, the Mexico City–based studio led by Mauricio Rocha Iturbide, has transformed the museum’s second floor into a space modeled after the shapono, the traditional Yanomami communal house. The works are set across modular walls in dark, earthy tones, lit by soft, filtered light, and the gallery windows have been reframed around the tree canopies outside, so “nature isn’t just an image on the wall, but an active presence within the space,” Rocha Iturbide explains.

Hakihiiwe began making art in 1992, when the Mexican artist Laura Anderson Barbata held a workshop teaching his community to craft paper by hand. That initiative eventually led to Shapono (1996), a book the Yanomami created entirely from recycled paper and thread spun from pineapple leaves. (Today, it is the earliest work in the ICA show.) Yet his relationship to art goes back to his childhood, when he watched his mother, an artisan, weave and paint baskets. “She taught me how to paint,” he notes, “and words she once shared with me remain deeply important: ‘This is the path for you; you must not abandon it. In time, you will see how well things turn out.’”.

Heeding his mother’s words, Hakihiiwe made art his life’s work, slowly shaping a visual language for Yanomami life and culture. To this day, he often creates paintings and prints on paper made from plant fibers or trees from his homeland. He first exhibited in Caracas in 2010, after which his work traveled the world, even reaching both the Venice Biennale and the Biennale of Sydney in 2022.

At the ICA exhibition, the artist’s near-taxonomic approach, rooted in close observation and repetition, is on striking display. One wall is covered with Kamie ya uriji pi jami Parawa ujame theperekui uriji terimi thepe komi kua (Donde yo vivo también viven todos estos animales en el Orinoco) (2018), a series of about 60 works on paper, each filled with repeated drawings in red and black ink. At first glance, they appear to be simple lines and symbols, a kind of script. Peer closer, though, and each gesture evokes an animal found in the Orinoco basin: rows of crab eyes, heron feet, ticks. Tarara (Casa de hormigas grandes) (2023) plays with perception in a similar way: red acrylic lines branch across cotton paper like a cosmic web or a map of neural pathways. What they actually trace, as the title suggests, is a house of large ants.

The pared-back quality of Hakihiiwe’s works conceals an undercurrent of urgency. The Amazon shelters much of Earth’s plant and animal life, absorbs vast amounts of carbon, and shapes weather far beyond its borders. But illegal mining, deforestation, pollution, and climate change have left it at serious risk. (Scientists estimate that about 20% of the rainforest has disappeared over the past 50 years.) “Hakihiiwe calls our attention to the ecological crisis affecting the Amazon forest, reminding us that we are all together in this problem, on a planetary scale,” says Michela Alessandrini, curator at the Fondation Cartier. “His take on this matter is brave, conscious, yet tender. His work is an vital reminder of the fragility of our planet, and a representation of the manifestations it grants humans on a daily basis, if they just pay attention.”.

Recent findings suggest that sheroanawe Hakihiiwe, He hupe (Mountains), 2026. Pigmented and pressed pulp on cotton pulp and screen printing, 76 3/8 x 152 3/4 in. (194 x 388 cm), diptych. Courtesy the artist and Galería ABRA, Caracas.

Elsewhere in the show, a series of landscapes offers a wider view of the ecosystems that inspire Hakihiiwe’s art. A highlight is the sprawling diptych He hupe (Mountains) (2026), made of pigmented pressed cotton pulp with screen printing that conjures the mountains of the Orinoco region. “Hakihiiwe always carries his native surroundings with him through his dreams and his art, wherever he goes… These mountains are constructed through layers of different techniques and colors, reading as an accumulation of dreamlike visions, memories, and natural elements separated across time and space,” Alessandrini adds.

It has been revealed that since Hakihiiwe assumed the role of shaman in 2024, dreams and visions have taken on a deeper meaning in his work. An crucial section of the show explores how the initiation has shaped his art. A fresh film, Hekura peni ware puhi aupouhe (The Spirits Wash My Face) (2026), sets kaleidoscopic drawings in motion to the sound of his own chanting, centering his bond with the spirits that visit him as he sleeps. An installation of three red shamanic poles, made on site, also speaks to the increasingly sacred dimension of his practice.

In a recent development, from the exhibition’s smallest ink drawings to the largest installations, the same elements return again and again. For the Yanomami, explains Gean Moreno, co-curator of the exhibition, all forms speak to one another: the cosmos to the patterns of ceremonial body paint, a feather crown to the shape of the communal house. “The pattern in the shamanic poles at the center of the exhibition space appears identical to the alligator skin of the mythical figure Irawire, who brought fire to the Yanomami,” Moreno indicates. “Rather than a logic of originality and representation, we have something like a circular movement of forms reiterating one another and reinforcing the overall cosmological whole at every turn.”.

For Hakihiiwe, the notion of a world in which everything is part of a whole has only grown more profound since his initiation. “Now I feel a coolness in my chest, like a gentle breeze passing through,” he indicates. “I feel more deeply connected to the spirits, to the wind, and to the living world, and that gives me an even greater desire to create.”.

Recent findings suggest that gordon Ramsay has earned 17 Michelin stars throughout his career and still oversees nearly 100 restaurants. This is a man who’s never met a goalpost he didn’t want to surpass. So it wasn’t entirely surprising when he posted a bare-chested shot of his six-pack to the grid earlier this month. What generated headlines was the occasion: his 60th birthday. “Gordon Ramsay thirst trap was not on my bingo card,” reads one comment. “My wife is on this app sir,” reads another.

Sources indicate that at home in London, he highlights me the Insights section on his Instagram account, which reveals the photo has gotten over 62 million impressions. “It’s very strange,” he states. “I’ve had a lot of ribbing from my eldest daughter, Megan. She’s a police officer. She was like, ‘Dad, how can you do that to me?’ All her senior sergeants and officers were laughing and telling her to tell me they’re going for a run. They’re in their early 40s. And then my Royal Marines Commando son just sent me a message with: ‘WTF dad, what are you doing?’”.

Recent findings suggest that ramsay has been a pretty active guy for a while now, despite working in an industry typically associated with chaotic diets and zero time for exercise. He was a youth soccer player back in the day, before becoming a chef and then, in his 40s, going from weighing 252 pounds to competing in marathons and Ironmans.

All very impressive, but it’s even rarer to be this chiseled in your 60s (maintaining a low body fat percentage becomes harder as your testosterone and growth hormone production slows down). Read on to learn more about his preferred forms of cardio, his favorite pre-workout treat, and why he's established a daily cryotherapy routine. “I call it my freezer,” he says.

Sources indicate that “15 minutes a day. It starts off with a quick two-minute stretch and 100 sit-ups every morning. Precore lifestyle is my ab cruncher thing—these things are fucking amazing, by the way. If I miss a day, then I have to punish it and do double the next day.”.

“It’s not physically hard with significant weights. These are 25 pounds. I’ll do a strength class once a week, 45 minutes. That’s it. Occasional push-ups and squats. No personal trainer.”.

Recent findings suggest that “What’s helped tremendously, with no impact on any of the joints, is a lot of swimming. So I have an injury in my patella, my right knee, right now. So I just increased the swimming because that’s the only sport that can use every muscle in your body with zero impact. But cardio is off the charts.”.

“I have a Zwift bike, so I jump on that for 45 minutes. There’s no impact on that. I’ll do that Monday, Wednesday, Friday and gear up for 90 minutes on a Sunday. If I wasn’t injured, I’d be doing three 5K runs again, Monday, Wednesday, Friday, 20-minute runs. I’ve got my 5K back down to 21 minutes. The dream is under 20. I was running at 19 and a half back in July. A 5K run is easy to do in the morning before work, it’s done within half an hour. Once I do that, I can gear up for either a two-hour bike on a Sunday or a 90-minute run. I alternate. So, one Sunday’s run, one Sunday’s bike.”.

“10 years ago, I ruptured my Achilles. I invested in an AlterG, a beautiful running machine that takes your weight, so you get all the cardio you want and less impact on the joint.”.

“From the chef’s perspective, I call it my freezer. It’s the cryochamber. I do two sets of three minutes every morning. I try to go seven days a week in that thing, straight after [working out]. That is incredible. That’ll get up to like minus 160. For six minutes.”.

According to recent reports, “I’ve invested in a tiny little red-light therapy sauna outside in the garden, and it seats two of you, and so [I’ll do] half an hour of that, every other day. This doesn’t need to be done every day. Three times a week’s fine. So when I’m not running, the other day I’ll sit in that red-light therapy and spend 20 minutes, 30 minutes in there, which is brilliant.”.

In a recent development, “The older you get, the more you have to stretch. I use a lot of bands. And so after sitting and stretching, I had those incredible bands where you lift your feet up and pull and stretch. 5 minutes is always a nice stretch before you [work out] and then 10 minutes stretch after that. I’ve never been to a yoga class in my life.”.

“I’m major on oatmeal for breakfast, Monday to Friday. I indulge Saturday, Sunday. I will do [oatmeal with] blueberry compote, caramelized banana for my potassium, and then fresh blueberries on top with some—it sounds weird, but it’s delicious—hot honey.”.

Sources indicate that “I have my friends at Precision. I’ll do one of their gels before I start that 5K, a protein gel, 30 grams, and then that sees me through the whole 45-minute routine. Coffee is just a full-fat, flat white, extra hot. Extra hot means I can sip it slowly. I cut out a lot of dairy, a lot of butter, a lot of cream. And so that treat in the morning with a flat white is that sort of, ‘I’ve earned this shit.’”.

“I don’t overstress on that because I stay fit. I monitor what I eat, but if anything, I’ll do smaller portions now. I’ll involve a lot of spinach, involve a lot of salmon, chicken, especially thighs. We’re just smart with less cream, less butter intake. And then when we travel, we just keep it light.”.

“I have a red wine with dinner, Californian, something light, something delicious. In 20, 30 years running restaurants, I’ve never gone around the room holding a glass of wine, holding a glass of champagne, sitting down, drinking with customers. Again, discipline.”.

“Just a couple of spoons of creatine, five mornings a week. A little scoop in my water.”.

In a recent development, “One thing I’ve learned in my 50s and my 60s—everyone said the older you get, the less you sleep. I think it’s the other way around. I like to be in bed by 11, and I’m up at 6. My Oura ring for me has become my best mate, because it just gives me the proper day-by-day indication and then keeps you on track for sleep.”.

It has been revealed that “No, no, no, no, no, no. Definitely not. No. I mean, no. My meditation is Kitchen fucking Nightmares. Dealing with some of those contributors on there and having to sit with them and talk with them. But no, not very good at sitting still.”.

A breakfast strata is one of our go-tos when we want a hearty, shareable brunch dish, but it’s hard to put into words how good this French onion croissant strata is. It takes a few extra minutes to deeply caramelize the onions, but the extra flavor and richness make a HUGE difference.

It has been revealed that chicken soup is a comfort food icon, good for the soul and the stomach, and there are a world’s worth of chicken soup recipes to choose from. Take chicken, egg noodles, some veggies, and a creamy sauce and bake them into a hearty casserole? You have a hearty dinner that leads to full bellies and happy hearts.

Slow-Cooker Cowboy Potato Casserole.

This slow-cooker casserole, featuring potatoes, beans, corn, and lots of cheese, is hearty, packed with flavor, and sure to make repeat appearances on your grub rotation all fall long.

Recent findings suggest that chicken and broccoli casserole is a meal that most people at Team Delish grew up eating, and this recipe is guaranteed to make you feel like a kid again. This creamy, cheesy, Ritz cracker-topped casserole is packed with chicken, rice, and freshly blanched broccoli with the quintessential cream of mushroom soup.

Apple Cheddar Crescent Casserole.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to this casserole, think breakfast strata with buttery, caramelized apples, and lots of sharp cheddar. If you’re in need of a quick fall-forward recipe to throw together for a weekend brunch, you can easily turn to this one.

According to recent reports, when we need a direct flight to a quick and easy dinner destination, we turn to two trusty options: a casserole or a chicken dinner. This chicken and rice casserole is the best of both worlds. It requires minimal cleanup, and the hands-on cooking time is only 20 minutes. The rest of the time, you can just lounge in your living room while this whips itself up.

When the weather gets cold, your dinner making-mojo is low, or when comfort food is just what’s on the menu, you need a casserole. Even though we have loved so many other casseroles before, there's always room in my baking dish for one more. And if that casserole is easy, creamy, chicken-y, and cheesy? With a crunchy topping? Our oven is already preheating.

Watch out, classic green bean casserole, gnocchi has entered the holiday menu. We took the classic recipe and added gnocchi for a dish that's infinitely better than the sum of its parts. Blanched fresh green beans and buttery sliced mushrooms, onions, and garlic get tossed with a creamy béchamel sauce and pillowy gnocchi, then baked until bubbly.

This enchilada casserole is what weeknight dinner dreams are made of. Classic chicken enchiladas are a fan-favorite meal, but they can be kind of tedious to prepare when you're low on energy (all that rolling, right?). In this recipe, you just layer all your components in a casserole dish, bake until melty and saucy, add your desired toppings, and serve!

According to recent reports, the star of any wedding-day look is undeniably the dress—however, the right accessories are an easy way to sneak in a little personality. Take, for example, the bridal clutch. It’s by no means an essential, but if you do choose to carry one, you might as well use it to add an extra-special touch to your day. From pearlescent minaudières befitting a beach ceremony to elegant envelope clutches ideally suited for City Hall, the best wedding bags both complement your carefully put-together outfit and act as an emergency catch-all for the little things you’ll want on hand, like lipstick and handwritten vows. (It’s never a bad idea to have an extra safety pin within reach, too.).

To narrow down a potential style for your bridal handbag, look for something that fits the aesthetic and theme of the wedding overall. For a city venue, this might mean a sleek, elongated clutch by Hunting Season or a structured mini tote by Le Sundial. Let your creativity run wild if you’re planning a destination wedding, perhaps with a hand-embellished piece, or keep things classic a leather envelope. Still looking for your something blue? A powder-blue clutch is a subtle way to honor the age-old adage. And if you want your purse to make more of a statement, consider metallics—gold and chainmail offer fun twists. It’s your day; you make the rules.

Ahead, discover 42 options designed to delight every type of bride.

It has been revealed that tasseled bags are having a moment, and the trend has even made its way down the aisle. Opt for a pared-back style with Marlies Grace, embrace your vintage-loving side with Anna Sui, or lean into opulence with JuJu Vera’s golden clutch.

In a recent development, think of a metallic clutch as one of your most key pieces of jewelry. Liffner’s golden design and Savette’s polished silver style are bound to catch the light just as a statement ring would. They’re also a great way to veer from traditional bridal white purses.

There’s no easier way to embrace the something blue tradition than via a clutch. Whether you prefer a paler blue from Self-Portrait, a cornflower-hued drawstring pouch by Prada, or a navy piece from Staud, a blue bag brings a necessary pop of color to your bridal wardrobe.

A satin clutch is perhaps the most classic handbags you can carry as a bride; its subtle shine flatters nearly every wedding dress fabric, from crepe to tulle. Choose a modern design by Attersee or a softly gathered pouch with floral detailing by Sophie Buhai—you can’t go wrong either way.

In a recent development, A clutch can be as much an objet d’art as an accessory. Simone Rocha’s micro egg clutch and Erdem’s mini bag with a rose-shaped handle both feel more like sculptures than purses. Let either take center stage against a minimalist gown for maximum impact.

Of all the bridal clutches, leather is the one you’ll likely reach for long after the honeymoon. Porto and J.Crew keep things minimal; Dior and Métier add a hint of gold detailing. Best of all, each slips easily into your everyday rotation, so consider it an investment that will earn its keep.

Industry observers note that looking to add an extra dose of glamour to your wedding-day outfit? An embellished clutch is an easy way to introduce drama. Altuzarra and Manolo Blahnik’s designs sparkle with allover crystals, while pearls on pieces by Valentino and Simkhai offer a more romantic alternative.

What kind of bag do you need for your wedding?

Recent findings suggest that something small will suffice here: You’ll have other people keeping tabs on the essentials, so think of this as a little extra accessory you can use to elevate your ensemble on the substantial day. White and ivory are classic choices, but gold, silver, or a pop of blue work just as well.

What should I put in my bridal purse?

Since this is an optional piece (many people tend to hand off things like cell phones and other bulkier items to their bridesmaids or members of the bridal party), it’s really up to you. Use it to hold the things you might need for touch-ups throughout the day, like lipstick or breath mints, or pop in a disposable camera for the after-party. The contents of your wedding purse are really up to you.

What are popular bridal bag styles?

A wedding clutch can be many things—and it doesn’t have to be a clutch at all. For functionality, pick something with a strap (like a tiny crossbody bag) to keep your hands free. If you do go the clutch bag route, choose something with embellishments to add some sparkle. Whether it’s shimmering pearls, iridescent appliqués, or gleaming sequins, these evening bags are your chance to go bolder on a smaller scale.

A Brief Guide to Grand Theft Auto VI’s Nike Sneaker Dupes

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 is finally out, which means we’ve got some in-game sneaker shopping to do.
  • Nike takes its name from the Greek goddess of victory, while Eris is the goddess of strife and discord—an appropriate choice for kicks you might buy with money from an armed robbery.
  • Industry observers note that the Eris Rise Low is the obvious starting point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is finally out, which means we’ve got some in-game sneaker shopping to do. We’d already spotted Air Force 1 dupes in the trailers, but now that we can finally play the long-awaited masterpiece itself, we’re taking a closer look at what else is on the shelves. There are tons of different sneaker stores sprinkled throughout the game, and Eris—Rockstar’s fictional answer to Nike—has given us a lot to work through.

Even the name is a joke. Nike takes its name from the Greek goddess of victory, while Eris is the goddess of strife and discord—an appropriate choice for kicks you might buy with money from an armed robbery. The Swoosh has been replaced with a pointier, upside-down logo, and plenty of the sneakers baring the mark are instantly recognizable.

Industry observers note that the Eris Rise Low is the obvious starting point. It’s the game’s AF1 equivalent, complete with the familiar paneled upper, perforated toebox, and a big, beefy sole underfoot. The Eris Strife 360, meanwhile, looks straight out of the Air Max 97 catalog. There’s the rippling upper, rounded toe, and long cushioning window underneath. Designed by Christian Tresser and released in 1997, the IRL sneaker’s silhouette took inspiration from water ripples, while the OG “Silver Bullet” finish drew on mountain bike components. Eris keeps enough of that shape for you to be able to spot it from across the shop.

Off-White x Nike Air Max 97 ‘White’.

Recent findings suggest that some versions get even more specific. There’s a white-and-orange Strife 360, for example, with oversized branding, contrasting lace loops, and printed side text that recalls Off-White’s own Air Max 97s. It isn’t a straight one-to-one recreation, but the reference feels pretty clear. An apparent take on the Off-White Air Force 1 Mid also appeared in the teasers. Someone at Rockstar is clearly a fan of Virgil Abloh’s work.

Then there’s the Eris Strife 90, with pairs that borrow heavily from the Air Max 90 “Infrared.” The bright red accents and sharp, aggressive lines are all there, with one colorway even adding black scribbles across the overlays.

Sources indicate that arguably the most iconic signature shoe of all time, the Air Jordan 1, gets a look in the game as well. The Eris Rook 1 High comes in leather and suede variations, with a tall ankle collar and laces running almost all the way up. There’s a black-and-white pair that swaps Jordan branding for an Eris basketball graphic on the tongue. You’ve probably got something quite similar in your closet at home.

Air Jordan 1 High OG ‘Yin Yang’.

It has been revealed that the Eris Cross Trainers are, well, harder to pin down. Available in several colorways, they have a mesh base and leather overlays. One white-and-gray version gets bright green hits that nod to Nike’s signature “Volt” hue. The simpler construction puts it closer to an older Nike runner, somewhere around MD Runner 2 territory, than a direct Zoom Vomero 5 or V5 Rnr copy. And for those times that tying laces feels like too much work, there are the very appropriately named Eris Basic Slides. The broad branded strap and flat footbed are very Nike Benassi.

Industry observers note that there are different versions to consider, too. “Origins” go all-white, while “Elite” options are matte and all-black. So if you‘ve found a silhouette you like, you can still spend another 10 minutes deciding which version works with your trousers. A problem we were hoping to leave outside the game.

In a recent development, it gives you an idea of just how much there is in GTA 6. The older games let you change your clothes, but here you’re choosing between different colorways, materials, and versions of individual shoes. And Eris is only one part of it: There are clothes and accessories that look like takes on Stüssy, Loewe, Chrome Hearts, and Louis Vuitton, too. You could spend a fair bit of time getting dressed before you get anything else done.

We’ve waited this long to play the game. A few more minutes in the sneaker shop before you really get going on missions won’t hurt.

A version of the story originally appeared on British GQ.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that squash and sausage are a heroic autumnal pairing, especially in a weeknight-friendly pasta.
  • Rigatoni’s ribbed surface and large holes help chunky squash sauce cling and bites of seared sausage and date wedge—opting for a nutty whole wheat variety will only add to this meal’s autumnal earthiness.
  • More cozy pastas this way: Balsamic Mushroom and Sausage Pasta; Creamy Red Curry Pasta; and Baked Feta Pasta With Green Sauce.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that squash and sausage are a heroic autumnal pairing, especially in a weeknight-friendly pasta. Butternut is the easiest squash to source—not to mention easily found peeled and chopped (a blessing for those with more timid knife skills). But other winter squash like acorn or red kuri can stand in as desired. Whichever squash you select, a sharp, heavy chef’s knife is best for breaking down the chunky veg. But to make your life easier, microwave the squash for 1 to 2 minutes. It will slightly soften, making it simpler—and safer—to slice through.

Rigatoni’s ribbed surface and large holes help chunky squash sauce cling and bites of seared sausage and date wedge—opting for a nutty whole wheat variety will only add to this meal’s autumnal earthiness.

More cozy pastas this way: Balsamic Mushroom and Sausage Pasta; Creamy Red Curry Pasta; and Baked Feta Pasta With Green Sauce.

Recent findings suggest that cook 1 medium butternut squash (1½–2 lb.), peeled, halved, seeds removed, cut into 1" pieces (about 6 cups), in a large pot of boiling salted water until very tender, 12–14 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer squash to a medium bowl. Reduce heat to low, cover pot, and leave on burner to keep warm.

Sources indicate that heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or a medium Dutch oven over medium-high. Add 1 lb. hot or sweet Italian sausage, casings removed, and break up into small pieces with a wooden spoon. Cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, about 3 minutes. Continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until browned all over and just cooked through, 3–4 minutes more. Transfer to a plate with a slotted spoon.

Industry observers note that reduce heat to medium-low. Cook 3½ oz. Medjool dates (about 6), pitted, sliced lengthwise ¾" thick, in same pan, turning halfway though, until deeply browned, 3–4 minutes. Transfer to plate with sausage; season with salt.

In a recent development, add remaining 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil to pan. Add 6 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper, ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and reserved squash. Cook, scraping up browned bits and smashing squash with spoon to break up, until lightly browned and broken up into a chunky paste (pieces do not need to be even), about 5 minutes.

In a recent development, meanwhile, return cooking liquid in reserved pot to a boil over high heat. Cook 12 oz. short tube pasta (such as rigatoni) until very al dente, about 3 minutes less than package directions (it will finish cooking in sauce). Drain, reserving 3 cups pasta cooking liquid.

In a recent development, add 1 cup pasta cooking liquid to squash and break up squash with spoon until a saucy consistency. Add pasta, another 1 cup pasta cooking liquid, and reserved sausage and dates. Increase heat to medium-high; cook, adding more pasta cooking liquid as needed, until pasta is al dente and coated in sauce, 2–3 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 1 Tbsp. sherry vinegar or balsamic vinegar. Taste pasta and add more vinegar, salt and/or pepper if needed.

It has been revealed that it’s an instantly recognized vignette: the San Jacinto Mountains rising in the distance, palm trees in the foreground, and a sea of mid-century modern homes dotted along the valley floor. Palm Springs is unmistakable, and its charms undeniable. It’s no wonder the glamorous desert destination has been a favored escape for Hollywood royalty for nearly a century. Beyond its numerous famous admirers (a roster that includes the likes of Elvis Presley, Lucille Ball, and Frank Sinatra) Palm Springs is also home to world-famous events, including the Coachella Music & Arts Festival, Modernism Week, and the city’s namesake International Film Festival. Where to stay for all of the above? The best Airbnbs in Palm Springs, naturally.

There are plenty of design-driven hotels throughout Palm Springs—there’s no denying that—but if you’re traveling with friends and want a home base where you can all be together (preferably beside a private pool), consider the Airbnbs below. Celebrating a special occasion, like a birthday or a bachelorette party? These resort-style vacation rentals also fit the bill. After all, they’re no ordinary rentals: Each of these homes tells a story that speaks to Palm Springs heritage, whether it’s a William Krisel estate from circa 1959, or an elegant property that once belonged to Katharine Hepburn.

Ahead, the 16 best Airbnbs in Palm Springs for a design-forward stay in the sun.

Positioned 20 minutes from downtown Palm Springs, this 1955-era home was designed by architect Walter S. White and is a National Historic Landmark. The iconic building is easily identified by its sweeping roofline, with curvature made to mimic the San Jacinto Mountains. There’s a cedar soaking tub for relaxing evenings, and a vintage record collection to set the soundtrack for long dinners. And if you’re a nature lover, take note of the native desert garden that encircles the property.

Amenities: Washer/dryer, AC, indoor fireplace, dishwasher, backyard, fire pit, BBQ, pool, hot tub.

It has been revealed that travel back to 1963 in this luxury home; it’s one of just a handful of original properties left on the block. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tuesday’s rout by Democrats has led one group dedicated to electing more Republican women to Congress to warn of a “crisis-level decline” of female GOP members on Capitol Hill.
  • Danielle Barrow, the president of Women for Women Action Fund, drew parallels between this week’s results and the 2018 blue wave.
  • Industry observers note that “After 2018, when Republicans lost 40 seats and elected only one new Republican woman, the party made a real commitment to recruiting and investing in women – and it worked,” Barrow mentioned in a statement Wednesday, adding that women accounted for 11 of the 15 House seats the GOP picked up in the 2020 election.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tuesday’s rout by Democrats has led one group dedicated to electing more Republican women to Congress to warn of a “crisis-level decline” of female GOP members on Capitol Hill.

Danielle Barrow, the president of Women for Women Action Fund, drew parallels between this week’s results and the 2018 blue wave.

Industry observers note that “After 2018, when Republicans lost 40 seats and elected only one new Republican woman, the party made a real commitment to recruiting and investing in women – and it worked,” Barrow mentioned in a statement Wednesday, adding that women accounted for 11 of the 15 House seats the GOP picked up in the 2020 election. But she cautioned that the party needs to sustain that focus across election cycles.

“Republicans cannot only make this investment after a wipeout election and abandon it when things improve,” she mentioned. “It is time for party leaders to treat this as a permanent strategy, not a crisis response.”.

Recent findings suggest that the ranks of House Republican women won’t plummet to as low as after the 2018 elections, when the caucus had just 13 female members. At least 18 Republican women have won House races so far, according to The Associated Press, and two others are leading as of Thursday afternoon. The conference is likely to see two new female members: Florida’s Sydney Gruters, the wife of RNC Chairman Joe Gruters, and Washington state’s Amanda McKinney, who holds a comfortable lead as votes continue to be counted.

Still, those figures are worlds apart from House Democrats, whose caucus will have more than 100 women next year.

According to recent reports, “We have always known that when women run, women win,” Florida Rep. Lois Frankel, chair of the member-led Elect Democratic Women PAC, noted in a statement Wednesday.

Those incoming latest members span the ideological range of the party, including progressives from New York and California who scored major primary wins this summer, to more moderate Democrats who flipped seats in Virginia and Pennsylvania.

According to recent reports, house Democrats had set a public goal this cycle to push their female membership past 100. Former Speaker Nancy Pelosi, who is retiring at the end of the year, noted electing Democratic women had been her “passion” since she joined the House in 1987.

“We made a decision to make more room for women at the tables of power – and generations of candidates, organizers and supporters have carried that work forward,” she remarked.

It has been revealed that blue breakthrough: Democrats flipped the House and Senate this week, giving the party one of its biggest nights in decades. On the Senate side, they wrested seats from Republicans in Texas, South Carolina, Kansas, Iowa, North Carolina and Ohio, while finally flipping Maine. Meanwhile, on the House side, Democrats were on track to not just win every race rated a Toss-up by Inside Elections but also pick up seats in deep-red territory that weren’t considered competitive until late in the cycle. Mary Ellen and Daniela summed up their initial election night takeaways, including how Democratic moderates and progressives both cheered the results and why many of Trump’s picks flopped at the ballot box.

Not going anywhere: The top Senate Democrat, Charles E. Schumer of Newly introduced York, is confident he will be elected majority leader by his caucus, especially after the party’s resounding midterm wins. Several of his incoming members have promised to support others, our colleague Savannah Behrmann reports, but the reality is there’s no real plausible alternative. Schumer’s own seat is up in 2028.

Redistricting rout: Republicans’ redistricting gambit hasn’t paid off as they’d hoped, the latest election results show, with the GOP appearing poised to flip only a handful of redrawn seats. Democratic incumbents who sought reelection from their reconfigured seats appeared poised to all win, although the race for Rep. Darren Soto’s Central Florida seat remained uncalled as of Thursday afternoon.

It has been revealed that taking the chair: Among the bruising defeats that North Carolina Republicans suffered this week was National Republican Congressional Committee Chairman Richard Hudson’s loss to Democrat Richard Ojeda, a former West Virginia state senator. Hudson is now the second party campaign chief to lose reelection this decade after New York’s Sean Patrick Maloney , who lost in 2022 while serving as the DCCC chair.

According to recent reports, upcoming senators: The incoming Senate Democratic class includes a returning senator, a former governor, two lieutenant governors and a congressman, a notable amount of governing experience. Meanwhile, five Republican House members are moving across the Rotunda after winning open Senate seats.

Member-to-governor pipeline grows: Five newly elected governors will be departing Capitol Hill to become the top executive of their state or territory, Savannah reports. Additionally, two former members who also served in the Biden administration were elected governor, though a trio of House Republicans fell short in their gubernatorial bids.

Comeback season: Roll Call’s Nick Eskow reports on the former members who are poised to return to the House or Senate next year, with at least seven winning comeback bids Tuesday.

It has been revealed that the firsts: Several candidates made history this week with their elections to Congress or the governorships of their state. Roll Call’s Andrew Menezes rounds up the milestone wins.

In a recent development, D.C. in the House: Robert White, D.C.’s newly elected nonvoting delegate, told our colleague Nina Heller that he plans to lobby fellow Democrats next year to support D.C. statehood. A potential selling point: The party could tackle affordability concerns better with two Democratic senators from the deep-blue District, he said.

Keeping count: As of 4:30 p.m. Thursday, Democrats had flipped 42 seats in the House and seven in the Senate, according to the AP. Republicans have so far picked up two House seats, both through redistricting. Twenty-eight House contests and two Senate races (Alaska and Mississippi) remain uncalled as of publication time. Check out Roll Call’s results tracker for updates as the races are called.

Indie losses: Independent Senate hopefuls running in deep-red states did not find success on Tuesday, even in races without a Democrat on the ballot. In Nebraska, former union leader Dan Osborn came up short in his second Senate bid. In Idaho, former state legislator Todd Achilles failed to dislodge Sen. Jim Risch, while Navy veteran Brian Bengs couldn’t topple South Dakota Sen. Mike Rounds. In Montana, where the Democratic nominee did not drop out, former university president Seth Bodnar lost to Republican Kurt Alme. On the House side, Alaska GOP Rep. Nick Begich comfortably leads commercial fisherman Bill Hill, though below the 50 percent threshold needed to avoid a ranked-choice runoff. With votes still being counted, the AP had yet to call the race at publication time.

In a recent development, not just Congress: The blue wave that broke Republican majorities on Capitol Hill also washed over state legislatures. Democrats are poised to hold new majorities in 12 legislative chambers, including the North Carolina House and Texas House, according to the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee, although some results aren’t official yet. The party also won governing trifectas in Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin. Meanwhile, in blue states, Democrats tightened their grip on government: In Rhode Island, Republicans are on track to hold just 10 seats in the entire 113-member legislature, while next door in Connecticut, the 36-seat Senate could have as few as three GOP members.

It has been revealed that blame game: As Republicans take stock of what went wrong for them in the midterms, Vice President JD Vance was quick to point to the Iran conflict as an insurmountable albatross. “The reason we lost is the war,” Vance noted in a lengthy X post. “If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. … But everyone knows why we lost.”.

But the tariffs: A pair of Republican former senators, Arizona’s Jeff Flake and Pennsylvania’s Patrick J. Toomey, both also urged their party to focus on the impact of Trump’s tariff policies. “Arbitrary and capricious tariffs directly raised costs for all American consumers,” Toomey wrote Wednesday on X. “Many voted for Democrats yesterday.”.

Staying put: Pennsylvania Rep. Brendan F. Boyle says he will remain in the House, where he’s poised to become the next Budget Committee chair, rather than launch a Democratic primary challenge to Sen. John Fetterman next cycle.

Sources indicate that bayh Bayh Bayh: A third generation of Indiana’s famed Bayh family won political office this week, with Beau Bayh’s election as secretary of state. Bayh, a Marine Corps veteran, follows in the footsteps of his father, Evan Bayh, who won the same post 40 years ago before going on to serve as governor and senator, and his late grandfather, Birch Bayh, who won three terms in the Senate. Indiana Democrats had a breakthrough election this week, defeating GOP Rep. Victoria Spartz, winning a second statewide office, unseating the speaker and breaking the GOP supermajority in the state House.

Sources indicate that A win and a loss: Nebraska Republican Sen. Pete Ricketts won reelection, but his wife, Democrat Susanne Shore, lost a special election for a seat on University of Nebraska Board of Regents, which governs the university system. Shore, who lost to a fellow Democrat in the officially nonpartisan race, was making her first bid for elective office.

In a recent development, bans on the ballot: Voters in Arizona, Nebraska and Washington state have approved newly introduced measures barring transgender athletes from participating in girls sports. A similar proposal in Colorado also appears likely to pass, although the AP had yet to call it as of publication time.

According to recent reports, roll Call elections analyst Nathan L. Gonzales of Inside Elections shares 15 initial lessons from the midterm elections, from the president’s “political mortality” to candidate quality and the power of personal brands. And, Nathan writes, as bad a night as it was for Republicans, it could have been even worse.

As Maine goes: The New York Times caught up with with Republican Sen. Susan Collins, who lost her bid for a sixth term in Maine. Collins, who had survived tough cycles before, spoke of getting “caught up in the Trump tsunami” and how she finally had her “Margaret Chase Smith moment.”.

Sources indicate that “These are extinction-level numbers”: Texas Monthly sat down for an interview with former state House Speaker Dade Phelan, who anticipated a down-ballot GOP rout but not the full extent of it. “MAGA needs to be dead,’’ mentioned the Republican, who led the push to impeach state Attorney General Ken Paxton in 2023 and then was targeted for defeat by Trump. He opted against reelection this year.

Corruption a top matter: The Associated Press reported that its 2026 voter poll found corruption at the top of the list of concerns for voters who helped sweep Democrats into power on Capitol Hill.

According to recent reports, tar Heeled: Among the states where Republicans suffered their biggest defeats Tuesday, perhaps none was more stunning than North Carolina, where they've so far lost five U.S. House seats and are trailing in one another and lost control of the state House. The (Raleigh) News & Observer looks at how maps “designed to deliver strong Republican majorities [failed] so spectacularly at that goal.”.

It has been revealed that support and discord: Michigan Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed’s sharply critical views toward Israel roiled the Jewish community in Michigan. But exit polling suggests most Jewish voters backed him, albeit in smaller numbers than they might have had a different Democrat run, Religion News Service reports.

That's how many House districts won by Trump in 2024 have been called for Democratic candidates by the AP as of 4:30 p.m. Eastern time on Thursday.

Twenty-eight additional Trump-won districts remain uncalled at publication time, and Democrats are at the moment leading in eight of those races.

The figures stand in sharp contrast to the start of the cycle, when there were just 13 House Democrats in districts that backed Trump in 2024.

Since then, several Republican-led states redrew their congressional maps in an effort to increase the number of Trump-won districts and improve their party’s chances of holding the House.

In large part, this effort appears to have backfired in 2026, with the Democratic wave cresting high enough to wash over dozens of Trump-won districts. Twenty-one of the 52 Democratic wins so far have come in states that redrew their congressional lines: Texas (six Trump-won seats), North Carolina (six), Ohio (five), Florida (three) and Alabama (one).

Congressional Republicans are holding leadership elections next week as they transition from the majority to the minority party. Speaker Mike Johnson is not seeking his conference’s top post, setting up a clash to be the next House minority leader. On the Senate side, South Dakota’s John Thune hopes to continue leading his party in the chamber.

Industry News: As an Awkward Teen, Grand Theft Auto Was My Escape. Now It Feels Like Real Life.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1694 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq
