Industry observers note that rep. Gregory W. Meeks, D-N.Y., and staffers cheer as House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., takes the stage during a election night watch party in Washington on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Recent findings suggest that rep. Gregory W. Meeks, D-N.Y., the presumed next chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, looks to bring resolutions to the floor to “immediately” end the war with Iran when Democrats take control of the House in January, he wrote in a letter Thursday seeking his colleagues’ support to become chairman.

The letter, which officially revealed his bid for the chairmanship, lays out his oversight agenda for the committee, which will also see considerable turnover on the GOP side of the dais.

Meeks and other Democrats have repeatedly forced votes this year on war powers resolutions seeking to end the Iran war, with a Meeks-sponsored one clearing both chambers of Congress.

But those resolutions have been nonbinding concurrent resolutions, since the 1973 War Powers Resolution only lays out a fast-track procedure the minority party can wield for concurrent resolutions in the House.

With a House majority, though, Democrats could bring binding joint resolutions to the floor.

In a recent development, beyond war powers votes, Meeks also promised public hearings on the war. He also vowed hearings on a range of topics including the administration’s Venezuela policy and “repeated defiance of Congress's constitutional authority over war powers and trade.”.

“As chairman in the 120th Congress, oversight of this administration’s lawlessness and corruption will be at the top of the agenda,” Meeks wrote. “I will continue to advance a principled foreign policy grounded in our values, including support for Ukraine against Russian aggression.”.

In addition to Iran measures, Meeks also promised legislation focused on “clawing back Congress’s proper role in the making of American foreign policy” and a State Department reauthorization bill that puts guardrails on the administration and protects career diplomats.

Meanwhile, the GOP side of the committee is poised to lose at least a dozen lawmakers — or about half of its members — next year between retirements and election losses.

In a recent development, the departures include longtime members such as former Chairman Michael McCaul, R-Texas, who opted not to seek reelection, and Rep. Scott Perry, R-Pa., the Freedom Caucus chair who lost his reelection race.

Recent findings suggest that several other Republican committee members remained locked in races that were still too close to call as of Thursday afternoon, according to The Associated Press, potentially gutting the GOP committee bench further. They include GOP Rep. Young Kim of California, the East Asia and Pacific Subcommittee chair who was trailing her in race against fellow California Republican Rep. Ken Calvert.

Rep. Christopher H. Smith, R-N.J., who chairs the Africa Subcommittee, lamented the turnover Thursday but predicted a lot of interest among remaining House Republicans to fill the void.

Sources indicate that “There will be many who will want to be on it,” Smith told reporters. “We lost some really great people. Yesterday I can't tell you how sad I was about friends who are now not coming back.”.

Jacob Fulton contributed to this report.

Chili Crisp Yogurt Chicken

📅 20 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (417 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Slather Greek yogurt and your favorite chili crisp on chicken thighs, roast in a hot oven, and you’ll be rewarded with juicy, tender meat with a delightful orange-tinged exterior.
  • More great chicken and rice recipes this way: One-Pot Chicken Thighs With Cilantro Rice and Beans; Spiced Coconut Chicken Rice; Nana’s Chicken and Rice Stew.
  • Industry observers note that preheat oven to 425°.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Slather Greek yogurt and your favorite chili crisp on chicken thighs, roast in a hot oven, and you’ll be rewarded with juicy, tender meat with a delightful orange-tinged exterior. But the best part of this sheet-pan dinner comes after the chicken is cooked: Spread cooked rice into the pan’s juices, then slide the baking sheet back into the oven. As the rice soaks up the deeply savory sauce, it will crisp in spots, creating a texture that’s somewhere between chewy-fluffy steamed grains and a freshly toasted pita chip. And when it comes to chili crisp, we love the iconic and easy-to-source Lao Gan Ma, but specialty brands like Fly By Jing are great too—just make sure the one you use is not too spicy, which will overpower the dish.

More great chicken and rice recipes this way: One-Pot Chicken Thighs With Cilantro Rice and Beans; Spiced Coconut Chicken Rice; Nana’s Chicken and Rice Stew.

Industry observers note that preheat oven to 425°. Season 6–8 skinless, boneless chicken thighs (1½–2 lb.) with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

Sources indicate that whisk together ¾ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt and ¼ cup plus 2 Tbsp. well-stirred chili crisp in a large bowl. Add chicken thighs and toss to coat.

Arrange chicken on a rimmed baking sheet and top with any yogurt mixture left in bowl. Bake chicken until deeply browned and an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of a thigh registers 165°, 25–30 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board or plate.

Spread 3 cups cooked jasmine or short-grain rice over baking sheet with chicken juices and bake until most of the juices have been absorbed and rice is starting to crisp in spots, 12–15 minutes.

In a recent development, meanwhile, whisk together 1 Tbsp. finely grated lime zest, ¼ cup fresh lime juice, ½ tsp. sugar, ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt, and remaining ¼ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt in a small bowl.

Industry observers note that combine ½ medium head of green cabbage (about 1 lb.), very thinly sliced, and a significant pinch of Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt in a large bowl. Using your hands, scrunch cabbage gently to soften. Add 1 small red onion, thinly sliced, 1 cup finely chopped cilantro, and yogurt dressing and toss to combine. Taste cabbage slaw and season with more salt if needed.

Slice chicken as desired and serve with crisped rice and cabbage slaw.

Outside, the city of Las Vegas is readying its streets for this weekend’s Formula One Grand Prix, when the world’s fastest drivers in the world’s fastest cars will tear down the Strip at 200-plus miles per hour. But inside Sin City’s hot spots, the starry F1 events are just getting started—and everyone at the SkinCeuticals Las Vegas Grand Prix Party quite literally had their (glowing) game faces on.

On Wednesday night, SkinCeuticals, as the official skincare partner of Scuderia Ferrari HP, hosted an exclusive bash at Baby Disco, the intimate, moody lounge tucked away within Zero Bond at The Wynn Las Vegas.

According to recent reports, with the space aglow in Ferrari Rosso Scuderia red under a shiny mirrored disco ball and a checkered-flag DJ booth, guests snacked on wagyu bites and gourmet caviar-topped chicken nuggets and sipped on-theme cocktails. (Also served: SkinCeuticals’s top-shelf favorites, including the P-TIOX and C E Ferulic serums, passed around on silver trays.) The model Kelly Piquet, partner of F1 star Max Verstappen, posted up on the green velvet banquette, as other attendees played around with SkinCeuticals-branded poker chips and cards around the room.

On the venue’s outdoor terrace overlooking the glowing marvel that is Sphere, actor Chace Crawford and his dad, dermatologist Chris Wayne Crawford, took a moment to enjoy the view. The two were doing a little father-son bonding—a perfect setting since F1 is “a male, testosterone-fueled sport,” joked Chris. As a Texas native, Chace (who also came through GQ’s Men of the Year 2026 party in LA last week) has seen the F1 Grand Prix in Austin, but he’s excited to catch his first race under the megawatt Vegas lights. “It’s surreal out here,” said the The Boys star, looking out over the Strip.

Inside, sportscaster and former Seattle Seahawk superstar Russell Wilson, a significant F1 fan, couldn’t wait for lights-out-and-away-we-go on Sunday. He’s attended F1 races in Monaco and Montreal, but he really digs the Vegas experience. “I’m racing around the track tomorrow night,” he stated, “so I’m fired up about it.”.

At 9 p.m. the party kicked into high gear as Alex Pall and Drew Taggart of the Chainsmokers took to the DJ booth, easing into their set, kicking off a remix of thesynth-pop classic “Don't You Want Me” then incrementally dialing up the heat until Taggart took to the mic himself to perform “Paris,” the DJ duo’s 2017 hit. When the musician Sooin, of the K-pop group Meovv, hopped into the booth to chop it up with the Chainsmokers, the room lit up.

Recent findings suggest that they closed out their set with some on-theme bottle service, as the Baby Disco crew made their way through the crowd hoisting magnums of Champagne and a strobe-flashing disco ball shaped like SkinCeuticals’s iconic serum dropper bottle. Time for the cooldown lap.

In a recent development, “I just want to say, everyone has really nice skin in here,” Taggart told the room with a grin. “Shout out to SkinCeuticals.”.

Chace Crawford and Chris Wayne Crawford.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Welcome to In Good Company, where we ring in the festive season with fashion-insider entertaining tips, expert etiquette advice, and the perfect editor-approved hostess gifts.

Sources indicate that despite creating elaborate floral arrangements for the crème de la crème of luxury fashion, Mark Colle prefers a humbler bouquet to gift. “If I give flowers to someone, I buy them at the gas station,” he says plainly. “They have a trashy charm to them that I appreciate.”.

Industry observers note that that irreverent sensibility sits at the heart of the Belgian florist’s métier: Flowers should shock and delight—and sometimes make you squirm. “I want people to be surprised most of all, which, with social media and Instagram, is becoming more difficult,” he claims. Take his collaboration with Glenn Martens for Maison Margiela’s spring/summer 2027 runway show. It was the punkier answer to Colle’s arrangements for Raf Simons’s Dior couture debut in 2012, when he transformed the rooms of a Paris hôtel particulier with a million blooms.

It has been revealed that for Margiela, he lined seven rooms with flowers at different stages of decay, with the blooms left to show their age. “I start with color, [that] is always the most important to me,” he notes. “Dior, for example. You have red, pink, and gray. But it’s a very specific red and a very specific pink. It’s maybe not so much about flower, but more about the color the flower has.”.

According to recent reports, it takes a sure hand to make flowers feel at home in a space—whether that’s a runway, a grand gala, or your dining room table—something Colle knows well. For arrangements, he looks to flowers with personality, like goldenrod, a bright, textural accent, or dahlias, whose many different forms can set very different moods. Colle’s anything-goes floral work has caught the attention of a who’s who of fashion heavyweights, from Saint Laurent and Chloé to Louis Vuitton and Prada, whose co-creative director Raf Simons first crossed paths with him while shopping for plants at his Antwerp shop, Baltimore Bloemen.

Here, Colle talks about choosing flowers, creating a mood, and finding inspiration in the unexpected.

Recent findings suggest that dahlias. They come in so many different shapes and colors. You can use them for something that resembles a medieval painting, but you could also use them for something that needs to look very futuristic, because there are certain typesthat have super-colorful spikes. But for me, it can be any flower, really. There is nothing that I consider ugly or unusable. It depends on the context or how you use it.

Nobody ever gives me flowers. But if I give flowers to somebody, I honestly buy them at the gas station, because they have a trashy charm to them that I really appreciate. And also, it’s not what people expect to receive from me flower-wise.

In a recent development, goldenrod, which over here is associated with something you would find in a gas station bouquet, so to speak, because it has no presence at all. But for me, that makes it interesting that you can use this common flower that people even almost look down upon into something very chic. That’s sometimes a nice challenge for me.

The holidays are a time for families to come together, but for Guy Fieri, they’re also a reminder of the loved ones no longer with us.

The chef and television personality posted a photo of himself and his late father, Jim, on Instagram to commemorate what would have been his 84th birthday. It’s been nearly three years since his father passed away following a long battle with pancreatic cancer.

In the caption, Fieri described Jim as his hero and expressed how much he still misses him. Fans rapidly filled the comments with condolences and support.

In a recent development, “Sending love on this special day,” one user wrote. On Facebook, another commented, “I hope your memories of your dad comfort you today. He must have been so proud of you.”.

Others shared their own happy memories of Jim. “I miss the stories and conversations with this man,” one person wrote. “He was the best!!” Another recalled, “Jim was a true romantic. I'll never forget when he made the rose petal trail for your mom.”.

Sources indicate that fieri has been open about how deeply the loss affected him. “I wanna call him all the time and ask questions, help me solve issues or celebrate the wins,” he remarked in a series of Instagram Stories last year. “Wouldn’t be here if it weren’t for him and it's hard to be here without him.”.

Industry observers note that birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays are still hard for Fieri, but he’s also found some comfort in his family. In a 2024 interview with Graham Bensinger, he said, “The funny thing is, out of everything that's happened, it has made me probably 10 times closer to my mom.”.

And judging by the outpouring of love from fans, friends, and loved ones in the comments, the Fieri’s can take comfort knowing Jim left a lasting impression on more people than just his family.

According to recent reports, this is a Japanese-style rice porridge known as okayu. I ate this every morning in the early weeks of postpartum after my first daughter was born. It’s what our family reaches for whenever we need a simple, nourishing dish that warms from the inside out. For the smoothest porridge, let the rice soak in cold water before cooking.

Industry observers note that if you have time, soak the rice, which makes the texture softer and can aid in digestion. Place washed rice in a bowl and pour in water to cover by 1". Soak at least 30 minutes and up to 4 hours. Drain off excess water before starting the recipe. The wakame seaweed, which you’ve probably had in miso soup, can typically be found dried anywhere Asian groceries are available.

According to recent reports, in The Fourth Trimester, we ask parents: What meal nourished you after welcoming your baby? This month it’s a cozy rice porridge by Eating at Home cookbook author Trinity Mouzon Wofford. Read more: Breakfast at Home, After Birth at Home.

Combine 1 cup short-grain rice, washed, soaked if desired, ¼ cup dried wakame (seaweed), 1 Tbsp. dried red shiso, and 6 cups low-sodium broth (any kind) or water in a large donabe, medium Dutch oven, or other heavy pot. Cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat (you’ll hear bubbling). Uncover and stir, making sure nothing is stuck to bottom of pot. Cover and reduce heat to low. Continue to cook porridge 30 minutes more (resist the urge to peek).

Recent findings suggest that remove pot from heat and let porridge sit (still covered) 10 minutes. Uncover and stir. Rice grains should be cooked through, broken open, and creamy, but porridge should still be fairly loose. Season porridge with fine sea salt.

Ladle porridge into bowls and serve, topped with toasted sesame seeds, toasted sesame oil, and/or thinly sliced scallions.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the finale is set to premiere in theaters across the U.K.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“All good dates must come to an end.” This is how Amelia Dimoldenberg revealed to the world, back in September, that she was signing off from her beloved YouTube series Chicken Shop Date. To officially say goodbye, she gathered a crowd that boasted past dates, friends, Latest York City crushes, and media personalities at Metrograph.

According to recent reports, what started as a youth club project has, over the last 12 years, garnered Dimoldenberg cult status and a devout following. The Londoner’s intentionally awkward and endearing deadpan interviews with stars like Cher, Paul McCartney, Billie Eilish, Jennifer Lawrence, and Daniel Kaluuya weren’t just entertaining, they also successfully re-contextualized the typical celebrity interview setup—with a side of nuggets, chips, and neon lighting in humble fast-food spots for a dose of levity. Whether she was asking Jack Harlow if he could read, matching Alex Consani’s frenetic energy, creating ear-worms with Louis Theroux (who could forget “My money don’t jiggle, jiggle, it folds”), or fueling romantic fan-fic with her off-the-Richter chemistry with Andrew Garfield, Dimoldenberg consistently created memorable viral moments.

In a recent development, the finale is set to premiere in theaters across the U.K. and U.S. on November 24, before dropping on YouTube on November 27. Final-season guests have included Jorja Smith, Noel Gallagher, Nemzzz, Role Model, and Jack O’Connell (a.k.a. Cook from Skins: every millennial’s formative bad-boy pin-up). But on this night, in Metrograph’s theater one, Dimoldenberg let a few people in on the secret before the rest of the world, revealing the last episode and the much-anticipated closing guest.

“It’s bittersweet, but I feel so ready to do the next thing,” Dimoldenberg told Vogue ahead of the screening. Sitting in the empty theater in a sparkling lace dress by Mandalay, she explained that the decision to end the show was 18 months in the making. “It’s been a process to get there. And that’s why I feel like this is more of a celebration. It would be a weird vibe if I was just sad,” she joked.

Recent findings suggest that for the Thursday night outing, attendees including Sean Evans, Richie Shazam, Jon Caramanica, Joe Coscarelli, and Gabby Bryan laughed and made fast friends over dirty martinis, tart margaritas, and Chicken Shop Date-branded bags of popcorn. As Dimoldenberg made the rounds, she lit up and squealed when Harlow sauntered into the room wearing baggy pants and an oatmeal-hued knit pullover. The two embraced with a warm hug, as Mel Ottenberg—who swapped his denim uniform for a slick suit—chatted with comedian Stavros Halkias. Eventually, the giddy crowd began slinking toward their seats for the main event.

Sources indicate that “You’ve become something of a celebrity, Amelia,” The New Yorker’s Naomi Fry remarked, in a short panel before the show. “I know, it’s so embarrassing,” Dimoldenberg replied dryly.

Sources indicate that the series was aired in its entirety, and as the final episode concluded, there was some unmistakable sniffling, and even some tears. The closing credits gave way to a swell of applause, as cheers for the star filled the room. “I think that final episode had to be about me,” Dimoldenberg confessed earlier. In hindsight, it all made sense. With a rom-com in development, which she’s also featuring in, Dimoldenberg has intends beyond the internet now, hoping to one day direct, too. It was a farewell that not only centered her trajectory as the show’s host but also closed the chapter on this part of her career.

The theater had emptied, and upstairs a party had begun. Guests stretched across leather booths, sipped on cocktails, and excitedly exchanged their reviews of the final episode. The only thing seemingly missing was chicken. Not for long, though, as chicken parm sliders soon arrived. All good dates must come to an end, but this one ended the right way.

Nigella Lawson’s Best Baking Advice Of All Time

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are few people I trust more in the kitchen than Nigella Lawson.
  • From the kitchen hacks you’d never expect (like swapping milk for boiling water) to the little techniques that make all the difference in your final bake, this is Nigella Lawson’s best baking advice of all time.
  • Cooking might not require exact measurements, but baking definitely does.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are few people I trust more in the kitchen than Nigella Lawson. If she told me to put sardines in a birthday cake, I’d believe her. That’s just the kind of culinary authority you earn after nearly three decades of making us hungry through the TV screen. The cookbook author and television personality is now dishing out advice on The Great British Baking Show—she made her debut as a GBBS judge in September—but it’s just a small window into her extensive wisdom.

From the kitchen hacks you’d never expect (like swapping milk for boiling water) to the little techniques that make all the difference in your final bake, this is Nigella Lawson’s best baking advice of all time.

Cooking might not require exact measurements, but baking definitely does. “I think every recipe has to be as precise as possible,” Lawson told Vogue in 2018. “Baking, you have to be really precise. If you’re cooking and it suggests 2 to 3 carrots, it doesn’t really matter because they can be different sizes. It’s not going to alter the taste.”.

So, you’ve never really baked before. It’s okay to start small! A three-tier chantilly cake your first day in the kitchen probably isn’t your best bet. “It’s important to go for a simple recipe. Read through the recipe to make sure you understand everything that’s being told to you at the time,” she said. “Look for a recipe that gives you an indication of what to do at each stage. This is what I always say to people: remind yourself you’re not running a restaurant.”.

Industry observers note that if you’ve been making your chocolate cake with milk, here’s your sign to stop. Lawson suggests swapping the dairy for hot or boiling water instead to “bloom” the cocoa, dissolve the sugar, and loosen the batter. The result? A crazy moist crumb!

Sources indicate that instead of using plain water when baking bread, Lawson suggests swapping it out for leftover pasta or potato water. “It will help the bread’s texture and rise,” she wrote on X in 2020. “Taste it before adding, though. If very salty, dilute it with fresh water and, obviously, leave any salt in the recipe out.”.

It has been revealed that it might sound weird, but Lawson swears by cream of tartar for fluffier, softer scones. “These are the best [ones] I’ve ever eaten, which is quite how it should be since they emanate from one of those old-fashioned cooks who starts a batch the minute the doorbell rings at teatime,” she wrote on her website in 2017. “Yes, I know they look as if they’ve got cellulite—it’s the cream of tartar, which is also why, despite their apparent solidity, they have that dreamy lightness.”.

Industry observers note that lawson’s genius baking hack? DIY self-rising flour. “Nigella tends not to use self-raising flour in her more recent books as she doesn’t bother to keep both plain (all-purpose) and self-raising flour,” her site reads. “Partly because keeping just one type of flour saves on storage space, and partly because if you don’t use self-raising flour regularly, then it will lose its raising power over time.”.

Instead, simply add 2 teaspoons of baking powder for each cup of plain flour. Sift the flour and baking powder together into a bowl before using (and make sure the baking powder is fully integrated), and you’re golden!

We’re all a little extra busy around the holidays, so if you’re planning a dinner party or holiday get-together, it’s okay to make shortcuts. Even Lawson says not everything has to be baked from scratch.

Recent findings suggest that “I have a bit of a weakness for this sort of cake, which is essentially an assembly-job number, a construction of alternate layers of a rich, boozy cream and some store-bought sponge or other,” she told the BBC in 2023 about one of her favorite holiday desserts. “Here the layers comprise a confection of cream and mascarpone, seasonally spiked with Advocaat, full of crystallized ginger, figs and nuts, and that essential component of Christmas: gingerbread.”.

Even Lawson admits: “just the words ‘uniformity of size and shape’ make [her] quake.” Hello, crazy foreshadowing for her future on GBBS.

“I am not in the slightest bit insecure about what I can bake, and I’m so very happy doing it, but shop-bought perfection is way beyond me,” she remarked in a 2014 interview with The Guardian. “But I’m perfectly content with that, and with the ramshackle homemade-ness of my creations.” If that’s good enough for Nigella, it’s good enough for me!

How 4 states voted on election-related ballot measures

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1252 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that maryland voters fill out ballots at a polling site in Bowie on Tuesday.
  • More than 100 statewide ballot measures went before voters this week, including a handful that could shape future elections in their states.
  • Here’s a look at how those measures fared, including one in Alaska that hasn’t been called as yet:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that maryland voters fill out ballots at a polling site in Bowie on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

More than 100 statewide ballot measures went before voters this week, including a handful that could shape future elections in their states.

Here’s a look at how those measures fared, including one in Alaska that hasn’t been called as yet:.

Voters in Maryland on Tuesday approved an amendment to the state’s constitution that will make it easier for the state’s Democrat-controlled legislature to redraw the congressional map for the 2028 elections.

In a recent development, the outcome was a victory for Democrats, who could potentially eliminate the state’s lone Republican-held seat – the 1st District on Maryland’s Eastern Shore, represented by Rep. Andy Harris, the chair of the hard-line conservative House Freedom Caucus.

The Old Line State emerged as a bright spot in Democrats’ blueprint to counter the redistricting wars initiated by President Donald Trump and turbocharged by the spring Supreme Court ruling that diluted Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act and set off a slew of Republican-led map-remaking across the South.

But those GOP-led efforts appeared to backfire this week, with Democrats holding many of the redrawn seats in states such as Texas, Florida, Alabama and North Carolina.

Still, Maryland Gov. Wes Moore told reporters Wednesday that he was “ready to engage” with the legislature on a latest map, citing the threat of further redistricting in Republican states.

“Donald Trump is not done. He has already been very clear about his intention to go after additional states, to go after places like Mississippi and South Carolina and Indiana,” Moore mentioned, according to video posted by WBAL-TV 11 News.

Following an unsuccessful attempt to redraw the Maryland map in February, Moore called a special August legislative session during which state lawmakers voted to put the redistricting amendment, known as Question 3, on the November ballot.

The move faced immediate legal challenges from Republicans. Two Maryland courts ruled to block the measure from appearing on the ballot, finding that lawmakers had missed the legally imposed deadline to refer the ballot measure. The state’s Supreme Court, though, allowed the redistricting amendment to go before the voters, with changes to the ballot text.

It has been revealed that state and national Democrats campaigned heavily for Question 3 as some public polling pointed to skepticism among voters. Former President Barack Obama even appeared in an ad urging voters to approve it.

Voters in the Show-Me State overwhelmingly rejected a Republican-drawn congressional map that sought to dismantle a safely Democratic seat in the Kansas City area.

Missouri Republicans enacted the new lines in 2025, aiming to give them an advantage in seven of the state’s eight House districts, including the 5th District held by Democrat Emanuel Cleaver II.

A protracted legal and political tussle over the map ensued.

The group People Not Politicians Missouri started a citizen petition to put the adoption of the map to a statewide vote. While the petition effort was pending, the state held its August primaries under the latest lines. But in September, the state Supreme Court ruled that the 2025 map could not be used in the general election because of the pending ballot measure and ordered state officials to hold November’s election under the previous boundaries, first enacted in 2022.

Attempts to challenge the ruling in federal court ultimately proved unsuccessful, with the U.S. Supreme Court issuing an order that reinstated the 2022 map.

Groups on both sides of the ballot measure, known as Proposition A, reportedly spent millions to persuade voters. But St. Louis Public Radio reported last week that while opponents of the 2025 map were actively campaigning against it, organized efforts in favor of Proposition A appeared “nearly nonexistent.”.

Republican efforts to try again and enact a newly introduced congressional map for 2028 could be complicated by a constitutional amendment, approved by voters Tuesday, that curtails the power of state legislators to override the result of a voter-approved initiative.

Voters in Massachusetts opted this week not to join states such as California and Washington and adopt a nonpartisan primary system.

The ballot initiative, known as Question 3, would have replaced the state’s partisan primaries with an open primary under which all candidates would appear on the same ballot, with the top two vote-getters, regardless of party, advancing to the general election.

The outcome was a victory for the chorus of labor unions and progressive groups, including the Working Families Party, that opposed the measure. Holding so-called jungle primaries, the groups argued, could make it harder for candidates without financial resources or high name recognition to run for office.

A bipartisan coalition that included the NAACP of Latest England and Republican former Gov. Charlie Baker supported the measure, arguing that open primaries would give voters more choice and create more competitive elections in a state dominated by Democrats.

Alaskans weighed in this year for the second time as many cycles on a ballot measure to revert to partisan primaries and repeal the state's top-four ranked choice voting system.

With over 70 percent of the vote in, The Associated Press had yet to call the ballot initiative, known as Measure 2, which would also roll back certain campaign finance disclosure requirements. As of Thursday evening, the “no” side, which supports keeping the current election system, was narrowly ahead. The state has until Nov. 18 to finish counting outstanding ballots.

Recent findings suggest that under Alaska’s voting system, all candidates run on the same ballot during the primary. Then the top four candidates, regardless of party, advance to the general election, which is decided by ranked choice voting if no one takes a majority of the vote.

In 2024, Alaska voters narrowly voted to keep the current system in place.

National Republicans, though, have largely opposed ranked choice voting, including Trump, who has characterized Alaska’s voting system as a “scam.”.

Industry observers note that the state’s use of open primaries and the top-four ranked choice system has drawn fresh scrutiny this year. Outside groups spent significant sums trying to boost underdog candidates during the Senate primary in an effort to hurt the front-runners. And several candidates in the Senate, House and governor’s races dropped out before the deadline to finalize the general election ballot, again trying to prevent splitting votes with their party front-runners.

Sources indicate that then last week, the Senate race was upended by a Upcoming York Times investigation that revealed operatives aligned with the Senate campaign of Democratic former Rep. Mary Peltola helped recruit a candidate with a similar name to GOP incumbent Dan Sullivan in an attempt to stack the ballot with two Republicans with the same first and last names. The revelations have fueled an ongoing debate in the state about whether ranked choice voting encourages this kind of alleged campaign chicanery.

“We would not be having this conversation at all if we didn’t have a thing in place called ranked choice voting,” Mike Dunleavy, Alaska's outgoing Republican governor, told Fox News last week.

Recent findings suggest that dunleavy has ordered an investigation into the revelations, as has the Justice Department. The DOJ also sought to block the certification of the Senate result if the incumbent Sullivan loses. Last weekend, a federal court dismissed the lawsuit.

Alaska and Maine are the only two states that at the moment use ranked choice voting in regular federal elections, along with the District of Columbia.

Michael Macagnone contributed to this report.

Tech Report: Apple Juice Bread

📅 22 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (706 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level.
  • I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal.
  • Industry observers note that take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level. The subtle, but unmistakable, undercurrent of apple sweetness struck me as a bit of a magic trick in a bread that, otherwise, to the eye and hand was just a soft white loaf.

I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal. When I asked him what he did differently to prepare it, he mentioned he just took the same rustic bread recipe he baked elsewhere and used apple juice in place of water. I was incredulous. That was it? The same amount? The same technique? Yes and yes, he said. I was hooked. It turns out the water-to-juice switcheroo gives an added taste of fall without taking anything away from the shape and texture. It’s become an instant favorite at my house both breakfast and lunch, and I expect it will be at yours.

Industry observers note that take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed. You can do it!

More apple recipes here: 37 Apple Desserts That Make Us Want to Pick the Whole Orchard.

Mix 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, 1¾ cups apple juice, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 Tbsp. sugar, and one ¼-oz. envelope instant yeast (about 2¼ tsp.) in a large bowl just until flour is hydrated and a very shaggy dough forms, about 1 minute. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit at room temperature 15 minutes.

Set a small bowl of room-temperature water on work surface for easy reaching. Uncover dough, dip your hand in water and stretch one side of dough up and over to meet opposite side; turn bowl 90°. Repeat 3 more times, turning bowl 90° after each fold. (This constitutes 1 full fold.) If dough doesn’t always stretch to meet opposite side, just aim for the middle. Wet your hands and shake off excess water any time dough begins to feel sticky. Cover dough and let sit 30 minutes (set a timer). Repeat folding process to make 1 full fold. Re-cover and let dough sit another 30 minutes. Repeat folding process and resting one more time. By the last fold, dough should be significantly smoother and tighter.

Transfer dough to a generously floured surface, dust with flour, and shape into a tight ball. Dust dough with more flour. Dust a kitchen towel with flour and place inside a high-sided bowl to line. Arrange dough, seam side up, in bowl on top of towel. Tightly cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit in a warm spot until puffy, about 45 minutes.

Industry observers note that place a rack in middle of oven, then set a large ovenproof Dutch oven with a lid on it; preheat oven to 400°. Place a 12" square of parchment paper on a flat surface. Cut a 2"-long slit in each corner toward the center. Very carefully, tip dough out onto center of parchment, trying your best not to deflate it or ruin its shape. (It’s easiest to place parchment on a flat plate so you can easily turn dough out of bowl.) Working very promptly and using a pair of kitchen shears lightly coated in vegetable oil, cut an X in center of bread. Remove pot from oven and very carefully lower dough into pot. Cover pot and return to oven.

In a recent development, bake bread 35 minutes. Uncover pot, reduce oven temperature to 375°, and continue to bake bread until crust is deeply browned, 35–40 minutes more. Carefully tip loaf out onto a wire rack and let cool at least 1 hour before slicing.

Do Ahead: Bread can be baked 3 days ahead. Let cool completely; store airtight at room temperature.

#146097. The Under-The-Radar Brands the Best Dressed List Loved in 2026

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1906 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vogue ↗ Open Full Page

The Under-The-Radar Brands the Best Dressed List Loved in 2026

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1906 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Vogue’s 2026 best dressed list certainly knows its way around a luxury label ambassadorship: Chanel swans, Saint Laurent savants, Dior devotees, Miu Miu girls and Prada protégés.
  • The distinction between under-the-radar and fashion-crowd famous is becoming increasingly blurred.
  • Greta Lee, Hunter Schafer, and Whitney Peak have embraced the retro-futurist designs of Zane Li’s Lii, the award-winning label crafted from his unassuming and tiny Chinatown studio.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vogue’s 2026 best dressed list certainly knows its way around a luxury label ambassadorship: Chanel swans, Saint Laurent savants, Dior devotees, Miu Miu girls and Prada protégés. But along the way, you’ll find that some of this year’s most thrilling moments for ‘stepping out’ and ‘stunning’ (as per the celebrity style news cycle) came courtesy of designers whose names aren’t quite so familiar. For this particularly discerning crowd, an emerging designer and an IYKYK label carries just a bit more sartorial currency.

The distinction between under-the-radar and fashion-crowd famous is becoming increasingly blurred. Designers like Conner Ives and Rachel Scott’s Diotima have developed considerable celebrity followings and their fair share of viral moments, while labels like Kallmeyer are hardly insider secrets anymore. The next generation, however, is hot on their heels.

Greta Lee, Hunter Schafer, and Whitney Peak have embraced the retro-futurist designs of Zane Li’s Lii, the award-winning label crafted from his unassuming and tiny Chinatown studio. Tessa Thompson, Ayo Edebiri, and Paloma Elsesser, meanwhile, found plenty to love in Giovanna Flores’s free-form silhouettes, pattern agnosticism, and deadstock materials. Elsewhere, Elle Fanning indulged in the character play of August Barron, Jenna Ortega put a young designer’s extraordinary corsetry craftsmanship on the red carpet, and John Malkovich looked to upcycled lace. Rosalía has made something of a habit of championing emerging talent, with the likes of Yasmina Atta and Laura Andraschko finding a place in her expansive, prima ballerina meets bad-girl Mary Magdalene wardrobe.

Sources indicate that more than a passing fascination with the next big thing, this year’s best dressed list has fostered relationships with designers in ways that speak to their genuine curiosity and enthusiasm about clothes, the people making them, and the exciting places fashion is heading. Below, the under-the-radar brands this year’s best dressed loved.

Greta lee wears Giovanna Flores.

Industry observers note that brooklyn-based Giovanna Flores is a fast favorite among Hollywood’s most adventurous dressers for her scavenger-chic designs. Her work is often made using deadstock and recycled textiles, and utilizes unexpected fabric combinations, patchworking, and inventive draping. Paloma Elsesser dropped her polka dot bodice and zebra-hemmed G.F. fit amid one fab Instagram dump, and Tessa Thompson mixed her prints with a sumptuous Bordeaux sash. Ayo Edebiri opted for a mismatched strawberry seed and gingham number, while Greta Lee wore some canary yellow velvet. (Both Edebiri and Lee are styled by Danielle Goldberg and hold Chanel and Dior ambassador titles respectively—Flores’s spliced-and-diced one-of-ones are a must-have.).

Zane Li’s Lii is a fashion-crowd secret hiding in plain sight; this year, he netted the LVMH Karl Lagerfeld Prize for Innovation and was a CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund winner. Known for its architectural minimalism and precise construction in enchanting color combos, the Latest York label has struck a major chord. Greta Lee, again, was an early champion, most recently wearing an architectural two-toned blue dress with a sexy thigh-high slit. Whitney Peak wore a twisted tank and skirt look fresh from the spring 2027 runway—a collection that unspooled the emotional threads between girlhood and womanhood, reflected in dramatically skewed tops and miniskirts in scuba materials and wide-eyed shades of teal and tomato. Hunter Schafer has incorporated the retro-futurist designs into her ongoing Blade Runner 2099 press tour. Consider Lii a modern fixture in the wardrobes of Hollywood’s experimental minimalists.

Another Yasmina Atta custom design.

According to recent reports, rosalía has spent the last year either en pointe or expounding the possibilities of a popstar’s wardrobe, oscillating between the ecclesiastical and the balletic. London-based, Nigerian-born designer Yasmina Atta, a Central Saint Martins graduate whose surrealist designs draw on African cinema, folklore, and subculture, was central to one of Rosalía’s most viral fashion moments. This was when she stepped out in Newly introduced York in a custom Atta creation: a plunging, sheer bronze latex bodice, visible black lace lingerie, a dramatically dropped waist, and a frothy cream tutu, all cinched with studded belts—a look partly inspired by Edgar Degas’s Little Dancer Aged Fourteen. (Rosalía had also worn a slate-gray wool minidress by the designer earlier in the year.) For a musician whose Lux era has been defined by religious iconography and the discipline of dance, Atta’s fantastical yet fervent approach to fashion is a perfect fit.

Rosalia wears Laura Andraschko.

Laura Andraschko’s hedonistic, subculture-informed designs also found a fan in Rosalía. The Berlin- and Vienna-raised Central Saint Martins graduate draws on various influences: indie sleaze and nightlife, aristocrats, Sloane Rangers, and Alpine bunny glam. Rosalía has worn the designer on several occasions: at the 2026 US Open, she chose an Andraschko T-shirt, while a previous Paris outing saw her in a khaki minidress from the fall 2025 Après Ski collection, with a dramatic furry hem and velvet-trimmed, off-the-shoulder neckline. More recently, of course, she had to pull on a tutu-like skirt. It’s feminine and anarchic and exactly right for Rosalía.

Jenna Ortega wears Elias Matso.

Recent findings suggest that jenna Ortega and her stylist Enrique Melendez spent last year crafting a deviant glam-goth wardrobe for the Wednesday star. This year, we’ve witnessed a subtle evolution into freer experiments with color and textiles. For a Latest York screening of Klara and the Sun, Ortega wore a sculptural creation by young designer Elias Matso, made from steel corset boning and 6,500 beads, all inspired by the colors of painter Marc Ranger. The Polimoda graduate’s approach to corsetry is theatrical and technically audacious, with references ranging from Bob Mackie to Charles James. The custom dress reportedly took more than 300 hours to make, and marked a major red carpet moment for a designer early in his career.

“This dress was a massive test of my free will and just how much I was willing to put towards something that did not have a guaranteed return,” Matso said. “It was scary, I felt crazy at times, I lost a lot of money, and now this object exists. After many blisters, rebuilds, failed trials, international shipping nightmares, and working on it in six different cities with so many helping hands it just exists, and that is wild.” A hand-crafting corsetier to know.

Elle Fanning wears August Barron.

Elle Fanning is all about the Effie-coded whimsy right now, and Paris-based August Barron has proven a kindred spirit in this quest. Formerly known as All-In, the label is the brainchild of Benjamin Barron and Bror August Vestbø, whose designs play with heady ideas of domesticity, nostalgia, and the conventions of femininity. Fanning made a memorable appearance in a pale yellow striped polo shirt and a voluminous, bow-adorned tulle skirt from their fall 2026 Bedtime Story collection. The design duo has a talent for taking familiar clothes and articulating something thrilling throught them. Whether referencing American pageant girls, cabaret queens, housewives, gay icons Judy or a Marilyn, August Barron provides the much-needed glitch in the glamour for those brave enough to dial in.

In a recent development, london-based GOYAGOMA was the talk of London Fashion Week when the label made its debut earlier this year at designer incubator Fashion East (the same one that birthed Simone Rocha, Martine Rose, and Grace Wales Bonner.) Of course, Paloma Elsesser picked up his designs fast, and previous best dressed honoree A$AP Rocky is a fan. Founded by Bahamian designer Traiceline Pratt, a Central Saint Martins graduate who previously worked with Phoebe Philo and A-Cold-Wall, the label draws on memories of growing up in the Bahamas to reimagine everyday clothing through luxe fabrications, exaggerated proportions, and determined tailoring. Elsesser’s endorsement adds to an already growing list of admirers of the designer’s assuredly off-beat approach to the capsule wardrobe—expect to see it hit Dover Street Market soon, too.

Julie Kegels takes her bow during spring 2027.

In a recent development, antwerp-born Julie Kegels has established herself as one of the most interrogative young voices in European fashion, and both Paloma Elsesser and Rosalia have taken notice. A graduate of Antwerp’s Royal Academy of Fine Arts who went on to work at Alaïa, Kegels rolled out her namesake label in 2024, exploring the tension between conventional feminine dressing and something more surreal. Her collections manipulate familiar silhouettes through draping and distortion, taking as much inspiration from working girls as she does from furniture. Winning the 2026 LVMH Prize has only accelerated her ascent—her signature thong socks are an even speedier way into the brand, or you could hold out for her prepares to invest her LVMH prize money into the development of more shoes and bags.

Miyako Bellizzi styled and walked the spring 2027 show.

Sarah Pidgeon during a 6397 fitting.

Founded by Stella Ishii in 2013, with Lizzie Owens now leading design, Latest York label 6397 has built a quietly influential universe of lived-in separates and pieces that slyly riff on what “staples” can mean. Among its fans are Paloma Elsesser, Greta Lee, and Sarah Pidgeon. The brand’s debut runway show was styled by costume designer and best dressed lister Miyako Bellizzi, who also walked in the presentation. The downtown creative community has long embraced 6397, and this is the New York woman energy you just want to bottle.

Whitney Peak wears spring 2026, styled by Karla Welch.

London-based Torishéju takes an experimental and emotive approach to pattern-cutting and construction: trained as a menswear designer, Torishéju Dumi has built a sartorial world that plays with trompe l’oeil and other-century costuming made modern, combining subversive design twists and classic craft techniques. Whitney Peak, on The Hunger Games press tour, opted for a deconstructed scarlet red leather skirt brought together by sensual draping and thigh-high cutouts, paired with a sculpted black halter top. This is the one for those who like their fashion with a little friction.

Ayo Edebiri wears Still Kelly pants.

Never underestimate the power of a great pair of trousers. And as Ayo Edebiri knows, the best off-duty outfits often hinge on an immaculate basic. Her choice? Still Kelly’s tailored black trousers worn with a vintage Björk T-shirt sourced by stylist Danielle Goldberg. The brand describes itself as a sartorial “slow burn.” “Building a world, making good products, it takes time,” founder Marc Kalman previously told Vogue. “I’m cool with that.”.

Louisa Jacobson wears Catalogue NYC.

In a recent development, louisa Jacobson has never been one for fashion’s binaries. With stylist Edward Bowleg III, she delights in the push-and-pull of buttoned-up tailoring and daring exposure, masculine codes and feminine flourishes. Catalogue NYC is exactly the sort of emerging designer label that articulates that. Founded by former Peter Do designers Pablo Correa and An Nguye alongside Vincent Ho, the Fresh York brand approaches familiar wardrobe pieces with an experimental eye, proposing new ways of wearing tailoring and dresses. On Jacobson, those ideas find an exquisite home.

In a recent development, A saucy sliver of toe and a beckoning, warped heel have become immediately identifiable Jude signatures. The Paris-based footwear label was founded in 2024 by Jurgita Dileviciute and Denitsa Bumbarova, and the duo’s subtly subversive designs take familiar shoe silhouettes and give them a deliciously peculiar twist—most notably with their barely-there peep toes. Zoë Kravitz is a fan of the Date pump, while Sarah Pidgeon favors the Date mule. Tracee Ellis Ross has amassed a well-curated collection of Jude footwear, from the sinuous Fame pump to the Haze sandal. It’s little wonder the label has found favor with fashion’s freakiest feet: Jude knows that even the smallest detail can demand a double take at the dogs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chicken noodle soup just got way more interesting. Inspired by Egyptian bird tongue soup, this warming spice-tinged chicken broth is as comforting as it is flavorful. The real star here is the orzo. Toasted in butter until it’s deeply golden and nutty-fragrant, the pasta takes on a new personality. Unlike plain noodles, which quickly go limp in hot soup, well-toasted orzo stays al dente for longer, holding its shape and texture until you’ve doled out every bowl.

Any store-bought chicken broth, stock, or bouillon paste offers an extra boost of flavor to the base that chicken thighs and water alone can’t compete with—for an even more robust option, go for chicken bone broth.

More nourishing soup recipes this way: Curried Yellow Squash Soup; Broken Lasagna Noodle Soup With Spinach; Spicy Cod and Potato Chowder.

Recent findings suggest that season 1¼ lb. skinless, boneless chicken thighs (4–5) all over with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

It has been revealed that heat 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large pot over medium. Add 1 tsp. crushed fennel seeds, ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper, ½ tsp. ground cardamom, and ¼ tsp. ground cloves and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 20 seconds. Add chicken, one 1" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth or chicken stock, and 3 cups water. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Partially cover pot, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer until an instant-read thermometer inserted into thickest part of a thigh registers at least 165°, 15–18 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board and let cool slightly. Reduce heat to low and cover pot. Using 2 forks, shred chicken.

Recent findings suggest that melt 4 Tbsp. (½ stick) unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 1 cup orzo and cook, stirring often, until golden brown and fragrant, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 1 Tbsp. finely grated lemon zest, ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and remaining ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper.

Scrape orzo mixture into pot with broth. Increase heat to medium and simmer broth, uncovered, until orzo is just al dente, 8–10 minutes. Remove soup from heat and add shredded chicken, 5 oz. baby kale or spinach, and 3 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice. Stir until greens are just wilted. Taste and season with more salt if needed.

How Am I Supposed to Survive the Apocalypse Without My Phone?

  • Sources indicate that anyone who’s ever been trapped on a stalled subway or a WiFi-less flight knows how screwed we might feel without access to our phones.
  • According to recent reports, many found their way to Nomad, a pocket-sized device created to aid in offline situations.
  • Sources indicate that elsewhere, there are emergency libraries that you can download to your existing computer, with offline chatbots that can tell you how to find clean water or start a fire: lastbook.org, which includes how-to videos; Survival LLM, which offers up information from the CDC and FEMA; and Project Nomad (different from Studner’s Nomad), from Chris Sherwood, a prominent YouTuber.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that anyone who’s ever been trapped on a stalled subway or a WiFi-less flight knows how screwed we might feel without access to our phones. Last week’s tech outages––first, a failure of Microsoft’s systems, then, a national grounding of flights, followed by problems from Charles Schwab to Apple iCloud––were a reminder of how fragile our digital infrastructure is, especially at the dawn of AI. Preppers on Reddit, better known for discussing generators and the storage of food, began talking about how to AI–apocalypse proof the devices we’re all so dependent on. “getting serious about my preps with all the cyber attacks going on,” one user wrote. “I work for a security organization so I get a front row seat to a lot of the chaos. I’m specifically prepping for prolonged loss of power.”.

According to recent reports, many found their way to Nomad, a pocket-sized device created to aid in offline situations. “I had huge, huge spikes in traffic,” stated Jackson Studner, creator of Nomad and a student at Millersville University of Pennsylvania. (“I’m not a firm or a startup, just a college student who enjoys building useful things and sharing them,” Studner’s website reads.) With the help of his professors, he built Nomad to provide some entertainment on camping trips and cross-country trips with friends. They’d hit a dead zone, and realize they wanted to watch a movie, or run video game software. Nomad is a miniscule server with TV and films, the entire Wikipedia library, and portable Wi-Fi, and offline maps. “I really like the reliability aspect,” Studner tells me. “I like to own my stuff. It's kind of that simple.” He’s also added navigation for his new community preparing for the apocalypse (or at least a grid shutdown). “It will actually tell you how to go along the road, it can tell you how to walk there, it'll calculate times, that kind of stuff,” he said.

Sources indicate that elsewhere, there are emergency libraries that you can download to your existing computer, with offline chatbots that can tell you how to find clean water or start a fire: lastbook.org, which includes how-to videos; Survival LLM, which offers up information from the CDC and FEMA; and Project Nomad (different from Studner’s Nomad), from Chris Sherwood, a prominent YouTuber. Sherwood is best known for posting explainer videos showing viewers how to build their “homelabs”—personal, at-home computing devices—under the name Crosstalk Solutions.

The interest in Project Nomad, Sherwood remarked, has been overwhelming. “It’s got over 40,000 stars on GitHub, which means that 40,000 people not only saw the project and were on the page, but they clicked the little button to favorite it. And I'm getting over 200,000 views on the website per month,” he said.

Despite his upcoming fans, Sherwood himself isn’t a prepper. He was inspired by the Information Technology Disaster Resource Center (ITDRC), a non-profit that goes into disasters and provides internet services when they are completely down. “I had the opportunity to go on deployment with [ITDRC] when Hurricane Ian came through, and I saw firsthand all these people that were offline. It was a disaster. Getting people back online was almost as vital as the food and water supplies that were getting set up to help with the recovery,” he explained.

Industry observers note that studner wasn’t a prepper either–– at first. But since Nomad took off and he’s found himself in more “prepper” corners of the internet, his feelings have slightly changed. “It’s for peace of mind. I have my little go bag. I'm not too, too worried about it, but I like to know that if there ever was a real problem, I'd be okay in that situation.”.

You May Be Thawing Your Turkey Wrong—Here’s How To Avoid Spreading Salmonella

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (675 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Delish

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, thanksgiving is a marathon, not a sprint.
  • Frozen turkeys are generally the more accessible and affordable option.
  • In a recent development, making sure it tastes good is one thing, but ensuring that it's safe to eat is something else entirely.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, thanksgiving is a marathon, not a sprint. And the most involved, time-consuming dish is undoubtedly the turkey. The centerpiece of your holiday table needs hours in the oven and at least a day of brining, but don't forget the time it takes to defrost beforehand, too.

Frozen turkeys are generally the more accessible and affordable option. But they do require a little extra TLC and planning. So if you buy a frozen bird this year, you'll need to know how to work with it.

In a recent development, making sure it tastes good is one thing, but ensuring that it's safe to eat is something else entirely. Like chicken, turkey can spread Salmonella and other harmful bacteria. You should exercise caution at every stage of the process, including thawing, to avoid making your guests sick. Here’s what you should know.

Industry observers note that the USDA says it's also safe to defrost turkey in cold water, but in our opinion, it's not worth the hassle. The best bet is to thaw it in the refrigerator, where the bird can gradually defrost at the safe temperature with less risk of bacterial growth. What you should never do: thaw it on the counter, in the garage, or with warm water.

These environments are less controlled and can expose the turkey to the temperature danger zone (between 40°F and 140°F), where germs grow rapidly. Even if the center of the turkey is still frozen, the thawed exterior can become a hotbed for Salmonella by the time you're ready to roast.

According to recent reports, roasted turkey drippings make great gravy. But raw turkey juice dripping all over your fridge? Not so much. Even shrink-wrapped birds can leak, so you should always store your turkey on a baking sheet or roasting pan while it thaws.

Food safety experts also recommend storing raw meat on the lowest shelf. That way, any leaks are less likely to drip onto other ingredients in your fridge.

Industry observers note that we know you're probably keeping a lot of other ingredients in your fridge, so it can be hard to set aside extra room for the turkey. That said, it's a step worth doing. Giving your turkey plenty of personal space minimizes the risk of raw meat or its juices coming into contact with other ingredients.

Recent findings suggest that in the event that your turkey does contaminate another ingredient, here's what to know: Foods that won’t be cooked, like salad greens, should be tossed if they’ve come into contact with raw turkey juices. Cooking contaminated foods thoroughly can kill harmful bacteria, but you’ll also need to clean any surfaces the juices touched.

Turkeys are big, so they take a long time to thaw all the way through. The experts at Butterball say you should allocate a day for every four pounds of turkey if you're keeping it in the fridge. That means if you're working with a 16-pound bird, set aside four days just for defrosting. Once it's fully thawed, Butterball says your turkey will stay safe in the fridge for up to four days.

Industry observers note that and on top of that, brining can make your turkey even more flavorful. If your frozen bird didn’t come pre-seasoned, consider setting aside another day or two for that step. (Want some guidance? Check out our brining guide.).

It’s extremely important to keep things clean while you’re handling a turkey. One of the most common ways Salmonella spreads in the kitchen is through cross-contamination caused by poor hygiene.

Sources indicate that so wash those hands (including under your fingernails!) with soap and water for at least 20 seconds. Make sure you also thoroughly clean any utensils and surfaces that come into contact with raw turkey or its juices using hot, soapy water.

And above all, don’t stress! Americans prepare millions of turkeys every Thanksgiving, so you're not alone in your turkey-roasting journey. Follow the tips above to ensure yours turns out safe to eat and delicious.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • "We cannot afford to rely on outdated systems to oversee an increasingly complex financial sector," noted Rep.
  • A leading Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee introduced legislation Thursday aimed at helping regulators use technology to better spot financial stress turbocharged by artificial intelligence and around-the-clock payment systems.
  • Bill Foster, D-Ill., would require the Federal Reserve to work with other regulators to develop, test and publicly release model software that would improve the ability to assess market conditions in real time and respond rapidly to cybersecurity and other threats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"We cannot afford to rely on outdated systems to oversee an increasingly complex financial sector," noted Rep. Bill Foster, D-Ill., (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call file photo).

A leading Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee introduced legislation Thursday aimed at helping regulators use technology to better spot financial stress turbocharged by artificial intelligence and around-the-clock payment systems.

The draft bill, from Rep. Bill Foster, D-Ill., would require the Federal Reserve to work with other regulators to develop, test and publicly release model software that would improve the ability to assess market conditions in real time and respond rapidly to cybersecurity and other threats.

The bill is designed to help regulators keep pace with newly introduced risks "driven largely by the development of state-of-the-art AI models," according to a summary.

The legislation is intended to help regulators provide financing to banks during crises and wind down failing banks. The model software would reduce the amount of manual compliance work that smaller financial institutions would have to do by providing standard data formats for regulatory reporting and tools to manage and transmit the information to regulators, according to a Foster spokesperson.

“With advances in AI creating latest cybersecurity threats and financial risks, it's more important than ever that we modernize the way we monitor the health of our financial institutions,” Foster said in a statement. “We cannot afford to rely on outdated systems to oversee an increasingly complex financial sector.”.

Foster, who has a Ph.D. in physics and has been a leader on AI issues on the Financial Services panel, is in line to become chair of the Financial Institutions Subcommittee next year.

Recent findings suggest that he has been mulling a challenge to ranking member Maxine Waters, D-Calif., to chair the full committee in the new Congress. But Foster is now “leaning toward not running,” a person familiar with his thinking said.

Waters already has a confirmed challenger in Rep. Sean Casten, D-Ill., who on Thursday circulated a "Dear Colleague" letter seeking the support of House Democrats for his bid.

Casten touted his “career at the intersection of business, science and public policy." Before entering Congress, he worked in clean energy and co-founded a organization that converted industrial waste energy into usable power.

In a recent development, in his letter, Casten cited the need to lower housing and insurance costs, protect consumers from fraud, address risks posed by cryptocurrency and prediction markets and guard against the next financial crisis. He also promised to hold the Trump administration accountable for ethical lapses.

According to recent reports, he's got a tough road ahead of him, however. Every Financial Services Democrat except Casten, Foster and Rep. Sam Liccardo of California signed an Oct. 21 letter to House Democrats in support of Waters. That show of support came after Casten made it known he was interested and it was clear that Foster had been considering his own bid.

Although Foster may not compete for the chairmanship, he has recently talked to Waters about changing how the committee operates.

“He wants a variety of members to play a role in legislation brought up in committee,” the source familiar with his thinking remarked. He’s also seeking more input on witnesses who testify at subcommittee hearings.

The draft bill he released on Thursday covers a topic that Foster is likely to pursue throughout the 120th Congress. He often asks the most questions about the use of AI in financial services at hearings and offers the most amendments related to the issue at markups.

Under the bill, model software would be developed for banking records and operations, regulatory reporting, stress testing, anti-money laundering and fraud screening, AI risk monitoring and other activities.

According to recent reports, the software must be open source, publicly available and tested for reliability and accuracy, according to the summary. It would be tested using synthetic or legally permitted historical data rather than actual customer accounts. Regulators would not take financial or supervisory actions during the study.

The software developed during the study would not have to be adopted; rather, it “should be viewed as a starting point for further modernization,” the summary notes.

All software models would have to be published within one year of enactment of the bill and a final report assessing feasibility, costs and savings, competition and other criteria, would be due to Congress within two years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that this creamy, always comforting slow-cooked rice pudding is scented with cardamom and sometimes topped with nuts or dried fruit. Versions of it exist across South Asia and beyond, each one slightly different but speaking the same nostalgic language. I’m serving it with a little twist here—a brûléed top for that crackly crème brûlée moment, and a scoop of mango sorbet for brightness and as a nod to the classic sticky rice flavor.

Note: If you are not using a nonstick pot, be extra careful and stir every 4 to 5 minutes; otherwise the rice pudding will definitely stick to the bottom. In the event it does, swiftly empty the contents into a new pot and start simmering from low heat again. If you do not have a kitchen blowtorch, you can skip the brûlée. Serve warm or chill for 2 to 4 hours and garnish with saffron threads.

Find more Rachel Gurjar recipes here.

According to recent reports, to a medium heavy-bottomed nonstick pot, add 5 cups (1.2 L) whole milk, 1 cup (240 ml) water, one 14-oz. (415 ml) can sweetened condensed milk, 3 green cardamom pods, and one 1" (2.5-cm) cinnamon stick. Bring to a boil and add 1 cup (200 g) jasmine rice or any short‑grain rice, then turn the heat down to low and simmer, stirring often and scraping all the way down to the bottom of the pot to make sure the mixture doesn’t stick or scorch, until the rice is tender and the mixture is thickened, 50 to 60 minutes. Add ¼ tsp. fine sea salt and stir to combine. If the consistency feels too thick add, ¼ cup [60 ml] water and stir to reach your desired consistency.

It has been revealed that scoop the kheer into heatproof serving bowls and top each with 1 to 2 Tbsp. granulated sugar, ensuring the surface is covered completely. Then carefully brûlée using a kitchen blowtorch, moving in a circular pattern, until the sugar is melted and a deep amber color. (You want a thin, smooth crust that shatters when broken.) Top with a scoop of sorbet and serve immediately.

According to recent reports, most people might build an outfit around a pair of shoes. Others, around a jacket. But few, surprisingly, do it around a belt.

At GQ, we’ve always said that the overlooked belt is more than the sum of its buckle and holes. Not only will it stop your slacks from going south, but a good leather belt can make just as much of a statement as your shoes, and deliver as much of a stylistic flourish as a tie. Unconvinced? Enter: The studded belt. (Which, coincidentally, we're now increasingly seeing be offered by some of the most imitated brands in the industry, from Lemaire to RRL, Mfpen to Our Legacy.).

The charm of the studded belt is that it’s a vibe chameleon. Its decorative elements can pay tribute to any number of aesthetics, from Americana to punk to European artistry. And while any one will easily provide further flair to an already-singing outfit, the best ones also single-handedly bring even the most minimalist wardrobe to life. (And to be honest, that’s how I feel studded belts are best worn today: Against a white tee and jeans, for an easy win without changing your whole look.).

To help you find the right one for you, I've sorted through the vast waist-wear market to find a selection that won't just make your outfits sing, but set them on course for superstardom. See you out there, Stud.

Let's start gently: Somehow, Anderson’s has made a studded belt that whispers. It’s a small but mighty addition to their lovingly handcrafted Italian leather goods.

“If a stud falls out, make a wish,” is the outlook over at Htc Los Angeles—and they provide plenty of it. A true purveyor of the style, the brand has been specializing in rock-and-roll embellished leather goods since the ’90s. And they aren’t stingy with it either.

Trust Corridor NYC to come in clutch for all of your folksy Americana needs. The worn-in look of their studded belt—made in full-grain leather and tarnished hardware—carries all the tales of someone who’s worn it through the arid badlands.

If the fits over at the Ralph Lauren PoloFest in Tokyo last month have inspired you to join the RL tribe, any one of the many studded belts from RRL (Ralph's ranch-minded line) is a strong place to start.

In a recent development, as you’ll see from our list, Our Legacy—a staple for any serious fashion guy—has secured two call-outs. Here, they cut diamond studs to form a snakeskin-like pattern that, when worn against your best corduroy pants, gives the look some severe shine.

In a recent development, while we’re talking about studded belts as an easy hardware win, they're also the perfect place to score some color points too. Here, the green and orange mixes it up more than traditional turquoise.

In a recent development, since its founding in 2012, Maximum Henry has been handmaking our favorite leather goods right here in New York City, including their beloved oval buckle belt. But they also know how to do a good, uncomplicated studded belt.

Recent findings suggest that the floral studs on this OL belt aren’t merely decorative, but are punched into the very function of the eyelets. It’s a sweet look, really, and one done so effortlessly.

Sources indicate that dressing for winter, when all you ever want to feel is cozy, can leave you feeling like a schlub. There is, however, an easy fix in the form of the enviably Parisian stylings of Lemaire, who’ve released a brown belt with almond-shaped studs. Wear it with your all-denim outfit or heavy grey wool pants, it’ll make you feel like one of the brand’s cityslicking models in their closely-studied runway highlights.

While we’ve so far been paying attention to how studs can add some play, texture still plays a key role to make an outfit sing. A Kind of Guise made their turquoise studded belt with a tan nubuck leather.

Lemaire might be better known for their artsy fabrics and drape-y cuts, but their accessories department is a treasure trove too.

Florals can be a lot generally for most guys, but Mfpen uses theirs sparingly on their lean 2cm wide belt. Made in patent brown leather, it also adds a nice formal sheen to a dark winter ensemble.

We’ve so far seen how studded belts can sway from Americana to minimalist vibes, but we can’t leave out the heavy metal rockers. Heliot Emil shaves off the edges for something more digestible, but still packs enough punch to cut through a monochromatic outfit.

Finally, we've talked a lot about how to add spice to your fit, but what does that mean—really? Eraldo has some answers.
